**** WATER CONSERVATION PLAN ****
§ 50.50 NON-ESSENTIAL WATER USE RESTRICTION.
   (A)   The following restrictions shall apply to all customers or persons who
use or receive potable water from the City.
   (B)   (1)   Wasting water is prohibited.
      (2)   For the purpose of this section, the following definition shall
apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
         WASTING WATER. Includes the following practices:
            1.   Using potable City water for any purpose in such a way that it
flows, sprays, or is otherwise excessively discharged upon any street, alley,
or other public right-of-way, ditch, or drain; or
            2.   Failing to repair a leak in a system which delivers water
within five working days of the discovery of same.
   (C)   (1)   All swimming pools which are constructed after the effective
date of this section must be equipped with filtration, pumping, and
recirculation systems.
      (2)   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definition shall
apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
         SWIMMING POOL. Any structure more than 24 inches in depth and
containing more than 1,122 gallons of water, and intended primarily for
recreational use.
   (D)   New or replacement bleeder lines from evaporative coolers shall not be
larger than one-eighth-inch inside diameter. Bleeder lines shall not be routed
into the sewer system where the air conditioner runoff can be used to water
landscaping or other outdoor vegetation, except where this would be impractical
or unfeasible.
(1988 Code, § 4-3-13) (Ord. 2002-06, passed 6-11-2002) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.51 VOLUNTARY WATER CONSERVATION MEASURES.
   (A)   The Mayor or the Mayor’s designee, upon the recommendation of the
Public Works Director, shall have the authority to initiate a voluntary water
conservation stage. The following water conservation measures shall be in
effect at the times specified. The target to be achieved through voluntary
water conservation is a 10% reduction in daily water demand.
      (1)   Compliance with this ongoing stage is strictly voluntary and is
intended for all persons, firms, agencies, and corporations utilizing potable
water from the Municipal water system, with the exception of City-owned
facilities and grounds.
      (2)   City-owned facilities and grounds shall follow these restrictions
at all times.
   (B)   The following water conservation measures shall be in effect for all
users of the Municipal water system during the period of the year when daylight
savings time is in effect.
      (1)   Outdoor use of water through a sprinkler system or use of water
through a hose to water any grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation shall be
determined as follows.
         (a)   Users with odd-numbered addresses shall be requested to use
water in the above manner on each Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday.
         (b)   Users with even-numbered addresses shall be requested to use
water in the above manner on each Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday.
         (c)   Watering in the above manner shall be discouraged on each
Monday, as this is reserved for City parks.
         (d)   Newly seeded or sodded lawns or newly planted trees or shrubs
shall be exempted from these voluntary restrictions for the time period needed
to establish the lawn, tree, or shrub, which time period shall not exceed 60
days.
      (2)   The voluntary conservation measures detailed in division (B)(1)
above shall be in effect during the period that daylight savings time is in
effect and shall apply to all residences and to all businesses, agencies, and
institutions having grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation, and shall be
followed at all parks and public buildings which are watered with potable,
treated water from the City water system. Areas watered using legally treated
effluent water or irrigation wells are exempted from the voluntary
restrictions. Persons using water from private wells are exempt from these
restrictions, but are encouraged to use this water wisely.
      (3)   Beginning with the implementation of daylight savings time and
continuing throughout the duration of daylight savings time, outdoor watering
of grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation shall be discouraged between the
hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
   (C)   Agricultural irrigation see Cannabis Ordinances.
(1988 Code, § 4-3-21) (Ord. 2002-06, passed 6-11-2002; Ord. 2011-02, passed 5-
23-2011; Ord. 2012-03, passed 6-11-2012; Ord. 2022-10, passed 12-12-2022)
§ 50.52 DROUGHT CONTINGENCY PLAN.
   The following drought contingency plan shall be in effect at the times
specified. When Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, Stage 4 or Stage 5 water rationing
is in effect, no person, firm, agency, or corporation shall use any water in
violation of any provision of this subchapter. During Stage 3 of water
rationing construction water will not be available until the City is in stage 2
or lower.
   (A)   Stage 1 water rationing. When water use exceeds 80% of the current
maximum flow rate for three consecutive days or when short-term deficiencies in
the City's distribution system limit supply capabilities. The Public Works
Director shall have the authority to impose Stage 1 water rationing. The target
to be achieved by Stage 1 water rationing is a 15% reduction in daily water
demand. The following requirements shall be in effect.
      (1)   The Mayor or Mayor’s designee shall make public announcements,
through the print and broadcast media, concerning the Stage 1 water rationing,
whenever Stage 1 is in effect. The announcement will include a description of
the rationing restrictions.
      (2)   Use of water through a sprinkler system or use of water through a
hose to water any grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation shall be determined
as follows.
         (a)   Users with odd-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water in the above manner on each Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday.
         (b)   Users with even-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water in the above manner on each Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday.
         (c)   Watering in the above manner shall be prohibited between the
hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
      (3)   These restrictions shall apply to all residences and to all
businesses, agencies, and institutions having lawns, gardens, trees, or shrubs,
and shall be followed at all parks and public buildings which are watered with
treated water. Areas watered with legally treated effluent or well (private or
irrigation) water are exempted from these restrictions; however, wise water use
is strongly encouraged. These restrictions shall not apply to any person, firm,
agency, or corporation engaged in the business of growing or selling plants of
any kind.
      (4)   No swimming pools shall be filled. Swimming pools that were filled
before Stage 1 water rationing went into effect may have water added to make up
losses through evaporation or splashing. Water loss through draining or through
leaks in the pool may not be made up during Stage 1 water rationing. Indoor
pools used for medical or rehabilitation purposes shall be exempt from this
provision.
      (5)   Newly seeded or sodded lawns or newly planted trees or shrubs shall
be exempted from Stage 1 water rationing for the time needed to establish the
lawn, tree, or shrub, which time period does not exceed 60 days. No lawn shall
be newly seeded or sodded or trees or shrubs planted after Stage 1 is imposed.
      (6)   Plants which cannot be kept alive without daily watering may be
permitted to be watered from a bucket, but not from the use of a hose, on the
days when watering is prohibited.
      (7)   Restaurants shall provide drinking water to customers only upon
request.
   (B)   Stage 2 water rationing. When water use exceeds 90% of the current
maximum flow rate for five consecutive days or when short-term deficiencies in
the City's distribution system limit supply capabilities, such as system outage
due to the failure or damage of major water system components. The Public Works
Director shall have the authority to impose Stage 2 water rationing. The target
to be achieved through Stage 2 water rationing is a 25% reduction in daily
water demand. The following requirements will be in effect.
      (1)   The Mayor or Mayor’s designee will make public announcements
through the print and broadcast media that Stage 2 is in effect. The
announcements will include a description of the rationing restrictions.
      (2)   Use of water through a sprinkler system or use of water through a
hose to water any grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation shall be determined
as follows.
         (a)   Users with odd-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water in the above manner on each Wednesday and Friday.
         (b)   Users with even-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water in the above manner on each Tuesday and Saturday.
         (c)   Watering in the above manner shall be prohibited between the
hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
      (3)   These restrictions shall apply to all residences and to all
businesses and institutions having lawns, gardens, trees, or shrubs, and shall
be followed at all parks and public buildings which are watered with treated
water. Areas watered with effluent or well water (private or irrigation) are
exempt from these restrictions; however, these users are strongly encouraged to
use water wisely.
      (4)   No water shall be used to wash any vehicle (including fund-raising
car washes at commercial businesses), except at places of business where autos
are washed on every business day either with attendants, with automatic
equipment, or by self-service.
      (5)   No swimming pools will be filled and no water shall be added to any
swimming pool. Indoor pools used for medical or rehabilitative purposes shall
be exempt from this provision.
      (6)   Washing sidewalks, driveways, parking areas, tennis courts, patios,
or other impervious surface areas with a hose, except in emergencies to remove
spills of hazardous materials or to eliminate dangerous conditions which
threaten the public health, safety, or welfare, is prohibited.
      (7)   No potable water from the Municipal water system shall be used to
operate an ornamental fountain or similar structure.
   (C)   Stage 3 water rationing. When water use exceeds 100% of the current
maximum flow rate for five consecutive days or when short-term deficiencies in
the City's distribution system limit supply capabilities, such as system outage
due to the failure or damage of major water system components the Public Works
Director, shall find that the City is in a state of emergency and the following
measures are necessary to protect the health and welfare of the citizens and
shall impose Stage 3 water rationing. The target for Stage 3 water rationing is
a 35% daily reduction in daily water demand. The following requirements will be
in effect.
      (1)   The Mayor or the Mayor’s designee will make public announcements in
the print and broadcast media that Stage 3 water rationing is in effect. The
announcements will include a description of the provisions in effect.
      (2)   Use of water through a sprinkler system or use of water through a
hose to water any grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation shall be determined
as follows.
         (a)   Users with odd-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water in the above manner on each Friday.
         (b)   Users with even-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water in the above manner on each Tuesday.
         (c)   Watering in the above manner shall be prohibited between the
hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
      (3)   All watering of grass, trees, plants, or other vegetation at all
parks and public buildings owned by the City which are watered using potable
water shall be prohibited. Areas watered with legally treated effluent or well
water are exempt from these restrictions; however, frugal water use is strongly
encouraged.
      (4)   No water shall be used to wash any vehicle (including fund-raising
car washes at commercial businesses), except at places of business where autos
are washed on every business day either with attendants, with automatic
equipment, or by self-service. The hours of operation of these businesses shall
be limited to ten hours per day.
      (5)   No swimming pools will be filled, and no water shall be added to
any swimming pool.
      (6)   It shall be the policy of the City to keep Stage 3 in effect for no
longer than absolutely necessary. The Mayor shall take steps to lift the Stage
3 restrictions as soon as lifting the restrictions will not endanger the water
supply by reducing amounts of water in storage.
      (7)   Agricultural irrigation must be reduced by 35%.
   (D)   Stage 4 water rationing. When the inability to maintain or replenish
adequate volumes of water in storage to provide for public health and safety or
short-term deficiencies in the City's distribution system limit supply
capabilities, such as a system outage due to the failure or damage of major
water system components the Public Works Director along with the Mayor shall
declare an emergency and impose Stage 4 water rationing. The target for Stage 4
water rationing is a 40% reduction in daily water demand. The following
requirements will be in effect during Stage 4 water rationing:
      (1)   The Mayor or Mayor’s designee shall make a public announcement in
the printed and broadcast media that Stage 4 water rationing is in effect.
      (2)   The use of sprinkler systems and garden hoses to water any grass,
trees, plants, or other vegetation is prohibited.
      (3)   Watering of grass, trees, plants or other vegetation at all parks
and/or public buildings and property owned by the City from potable water
system is prohibited.
      (4)   Watering of gardens, trees and ornamental plants by use of hand-
held container that has been filled at a hose bib or faucet will be allowed as
follows:
         (a)   Users with odd-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water on Friday.
         (b)   Users with even-numbered addresses shall be permitted to use
water on Tuesday.
         (c)   Watering between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. is
prohibited.
      (5)   No water shall be used to wash any vehicle except at places of
business where vehicles are washed on every business day. The hours of
operation shall be limited to ten hours per day.
      (6)   Filling swimming pools and/or adding water to swimming pools is
prohibited.
      (7)   It shall be the policy of the City to keep Stage 4 water rationing
in effect no longer than necessary based on the criteria that caused the
emergency to be declared. The Mayor, on recommendation of the Public Works
Director, will lift Stage 4 restrictions as soon as lifting said restrictions
will not endanger the amount of water supply in storage.
      (8)   Agricultural irrigation must be reduced by 50%.
   (E)   (1)   Stage 5 water rationing. Customers shall be required to comply
with the requirements of Stage 4 of the plan, when the Public Works Director or
his/her designee determines that a water supply emergency exists based on:
         (a)   A major line break, pump or system failure has occurred, which
causes unprecedented loss of capability to provide water service; or
         (b)   Natural or manmade contamination of any portion of the water
system.
      (2)   During emergency Water Stage 5, the Mayor or Mayor’s designee will
make public announcements in the print and broadcast media that emergency
conditions exist and the nature of such conditions. The following additional
restrictions shall apply:
         (a)   Irrigation of landscaped areas is prohibited.
         (b)   Washing of motor vehicles, boats, trailers, and the like is
prohibited.
      (3)   Stage 5 emergency requirements may be rescinded when all conditions
causing emergency Stage 5 cease to exist for a period of three days.
   (F)   Winter watering. Hours for outdoor watering for the months of November
through March, from the end of and until the beginning of daylight savings
time, shall be on the regularly scheduled days between the hours of 10:00 a.m.
to 4:00 p.m. for Stages 1, 2 and 3 only.
(1988 Code, § 4-3-21.1) (Ord. 2002-06, passed 6-11-2002; Ord. 2011-02, passed
5-23-2011; Ord. 2012-03, passed 6-11-2012; Ord. 2022-10, passed 12-12-2022)
Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.53 ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   No person shall be convicted of violating this subchapter unless that
person in fact turned on water, directed the turning on of water, kept water
turned on after learning it was turned on in violation of this subchapter, or
failed to turn off automatic devices capable of turning on water in violation
of this subchapter. It will not be necessary, however, to present a witness who
saw the accused turning on the water, if circumstances indicate the accused did
turn on the water.
   (B)   The Public Works Director will provide monthly written reports to the
Mayor and the City Council while Stages 1 through 4 of water rationing is in
effect. The Public Works Director will provide weekly written reports to the
Mayor and City Council while Stage 3, 4 or 5 water rationing is in effect.
(1988 Code, § 4-3-21.2) (Ord. 2002-06, passed 6-11-2002; Ord. 2011-02, passed
5-23-2011; Ord. 2012-03, passed 6-11-2012; Ord. 2022-10, passed 12-12-2022)
Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.54 ISSUANCE OF CITATION.
   The Code Enforcement Officer and certified officers of the City of Ruidoso
Downs Police Department are authorized to write citations for violations of
this subchapter.

§ 50.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be fined in an
amount not to exceed $500 dollars or be imprisoned in the County Jail for a
period not to exceed 90 days, or be both fined and imprisoned. Each day such a
violation is committed or permitted to continue shall constitute a separate
offense and shall be punishable as such hereunder.
(1988 Code, § 4-3-19)
   (B)   Any person, firm, or corporation violating any provision of §§
50.50 et seq. of this Code shall be fined not less than $25 and not more than
$500 for each offense, and a separate offense shall be deemed committed on each
day during or on which a violation occurs or continues in accordance with the
general violation provisions of this Code of Ordinances.
(1988 Code, § 4-3-21.2)

§ 51.01 DEFINITIONS.
   The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall
have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context
clearly indicates a different meaning:
   BIOCHEMICAL OXYGEN DEMAND (BOD). The quantity of oxygen utilized in the
biochemical oxidation of organic matter by standard methods procedures in five
days at 20° Celsius, expressed in milligrams per liter.
   CHEMICAL OXYGEN DEMAND (COD). A measure of the oxygen-consuming capacity of
organic and inorganic matter present in wastewater, in milligrams per liter, by
standard methods procedures.
   CITY LIQUID WASTE SYSTEM. The sewerage facilities owned and operated by the
City for the collection, conveyance, treatment and disposal of wastewater.
   GARBAGE. Solid wastes from the preparation, cooking and dispensing of food,
and from the handling, storing and sale of produce.
   INDUSTRIAL LIQUID WASTES. All waterborne solid, liquid or gaseous wastes
resulting from any industrial, manufacturing or food processing operation or
process, or from the development of any natural resources, or any mixture of
these with water or domestic sewage, as distinct from normal domestic sewage.
INDUSTRIAL MANUFACTURING PROCESS shall include, but are not limited to, the
following: ordnance and accessories; food and allied products; textile mill
products, apparel and other finished products made from fabrics and similar
materials; lumber and wood products, excepting furniture; furniture and
fixtures; printing, publishing and allied industries; chemicals and allied
products, petroleum refining and related industries; rubber and miscellaneous
plastic products; primary metal industries; fabricated metal products, except
ordnance, machinery and transportation equipment; professional scientific and
controlling instruments; photographic and optical goods, watches and clocks;
and miscellaneous manufacturers or industries.
   INTERFERENCE WITH ANY WASTEWATER TREATMENT WORKS. Any condition or
combination of conditions that causes degradation of  the operational
efficiency of the wastewater treatment works.
   LATERAL SEWER. An individual user's sewer pipe, beginning at the public
sewer and extending to the premises actually served. The LATERAL SEWER includes
the stub to which a user connects. The term is interchangeable with the terms
HOUSE SERVICE CONNECTION and BUILDING SEWER.
   NORMAL DOMESTIC WASTEWATER. Waterborne wastes normally discharging from the
sanitary conveniences of buildings (including apartment houses, motels and
hotels), office buildings, factories and institutions, free from storm water,
surface water and industrial wastes. NORMAL DOMESTIC WASTEWATER shall mean
wastewater having a chemical oxygen demand less than or equal to 500 milligrams
per liter and/or total suspended solids less than or equal to 300 milligrams
per liter.
   pH. The logarithm (base 10) of the reciprocal of the hydrogen ion
concentrate of a solution.
   PUBLIC SEWER. A sanitary sewer that is controlled and/or owned by the City.
This is restricted to the main sewer line, whereas the property owner is
responsible for the lateral sewer line and its connection to the public sewer.
   SANITARY SEWER. The public sewer portion of the City liquid waste system
that collects and conveys wastewater to the wastewater treatment works, to
which storm water, surface water and groundwater are not intentionally
admitted.
   STANDARD METHODS. The laboratory procedures set forth in the latest edition,
at the time of analysis, of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and
Wastewater, as prepared, approved and published jointly by the American Public
Health Association, the American Water Works Association and the Water
Pollution Control Federation.
   STORM SEWER.  A sewer that carries storm water and surface water and
drainage, but excludes wastewater and industrial wastes.
   TOTAL SUSPENDED SOLIDS (TSS). Those solids, which are retained by a standard
glass fiber filter and dried to a constant weight of 103 to 105 degrees,
expressed in milligrams per liter, by standard methods procedures.
   TRAP. A device for retaining sand, silt, grit, mineral material, petroleum
solvents, grease or oil by gravity-differential separation from wastewater, and
of a design and capacity approved by the City Public Works Department.
   UNIT. A part of the property intended for residential, commercial,
industrial or any type of independent use, including one or more rooms or
enclosed spaces interconnecting, located on one or more floors in a building,
and with a direct exit to a public street or highway, or to a common area or
mall leading to a public street or highway.
   WASTEWATER. The used water of a community. Such used water may be a
combination of the liquid waterborne wastes from residences, commercial
buildings, industrial plants and institutions.
   WASTEWATER COLLECTION AND CONVEYANCE SYSTEM. The portion of the City liquid
waste system, including sanitary sewers, lift stations, odor control stations
and other facilities, that collects and conveys wastewater to the wastewater
treatment works, as now or hereafter added to, expanded or improved.
   WASTEWATER TREATMENT WORKS. The portion of the City liquid waste system that
accomplishes treatment and disposal of wastewater, as now or hereafter added
to, expanded or improved.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-1) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 92-11, passed 11-23-
1992; Ord. 92-13, passed 1-11-1993; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007; Ord. 2009-
05, passed 5-26-2009)
§ 51.02 MANAGEMENT OF SEWER DEPARTMENT.
   The control, management and supervision of the sewer system of the City is
the responsibility of the Public Works Director of the City.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007)
§ 51.03 USE OF FUNDS.
   Except as indicated under §
51.09(F), the funds received from sewer service charges and from permits to
make connections or openings into the public sewer shall be receipted into the
Sewer Revenue Fund of the City. Such funds received shall be used for the
operation, maintenance and extension of the sewer system, and for the
retirement of sewer revenues bonds as provided by law.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-3) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-
2007)
§ 51.04 CONNECTION TO SEWER; DISTANCE REQUIREMENT.
   It shall be unlawful for any person residing within a sewer district, or
residing at a property whose boundary is within 200 feet of a sewer line, to
fail to make connection with the sewer line with premises on the property. This
section shall also apply to owners of property who lease or rent. Failure to
comply with this section shall be grounds for refusing or discontinuing water
service to premises not connected to a sewer line.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.05 PERMIT REQUIRED; APPLICATION.
   Any person desiring to make connection with a public sewer line shall make
application to the City, on application forms to be furnished at City Hall,
prior to any and all excavation work involving sewer line installation. Failure
to obtain a City-approved permit prior to excavation constitutes a violation of
this chapter.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007)
§ 51.06 SEWER INSPECTION AND CONSTRUCTION-RELATED FEES AND CHARGES.
   (A)   Permit. Upon approval of the application by the Public Works Director,
or his or her designee, a permit shall be issued by the City Clerk, upon the
signature of the New Mexico-licensed plumber and payment of a tap and
inspection fee of $600 for each connection to the public sewer. The Sewer
Department will make the sewer line tap after line is exposed by the licensed
plumber. A street cut surface fee of $250 will be assessed for any project
cutting into a chip-sealed or asphalt-surfaced road (regardless of its
condition). These fees shall be paid at the time of acquiring the permit.
   (B)   Compaction fee and requirements. An additional street cut compaction
fee of $100 per square foot of excavation within the City right-of-way will be
assessed to the permittee if the plumber fails to use either City-approved
“engineered” or “flowable” fill, or prove, in writing (by a company licensed to
perform compaction tests), a minimum of 95% compaction on the filled excavation
upon completion. This will be assessed if City Hall is not provided with proof
of either within 14 days of excavation closure, and is intended to cover the
cost for the City.
   (C)   Connection. Once a permit for connection to the City sewer system has
been obtained, the New Mexico-licensed plumber on the City permit shall be the
only company authorized to perform such work. All work shall be accomplished
under the supervision of the City Public Works Director, who has the authority
to stop the project and require appropriate corrective action.
   (D)   Service restrictions. Except as authorized by the Governing Body, a
sewer or water service shall only serve one building, structure or private
residence when such building, structure or private residence occupies land that
may be subject to subdivision due to its size, and has sufficient frontage
along a public right-of-way to allow driveways to subsequent lot divisions.
Privately owned and operated, master-metered mobile home parks, apartment
complexes and gated communities shall be exempted. The City may disconnect the
sewer and water service to any customer where such service has been extended in
violation of this code, and continue such disconnection so long as the
violation continues.
   (E)   Maintenance. Use of the City sewer system shall be on a rental basis,
with a regular monthly sewer maintenance charge assessed against each user of
the sewer system as specified below.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007; Ord. 2011-02, passed 5-23-2011)
§ 51.07 PROHIBITED DISCHARGE.
   (A)   Purpose and scope. This sections deals with general sewer use
requirements and with the rules and regulations promulgated under P.L.92-500
relative to industrial wastes.
   (B)   Discharge of runoff or groundwater. No person shall discharge or cause
to be discharged any storm water, surface water, ground water, roof runoff or
subsurface drainage to any sanitary sewer. Storm water and all other unpolluted
drainage shall be discharged to such sewers as are specifically designated as
storm sewers, or not a natural outlet approved by the City.
   (C)   Prohibited discharges. No person shall discharge or cause to be
discharged any of the following described liquids or wastes into any public
sewers:
      (1)   Any gasoline, benzene, naphtha, fuel oil or other flammable or
explosive liquid, solid or gas.
      (2)   Any waters or wastes containing toxic or poisonous solids, liquids
or gases in sufficient quantity, either singly or by interaction with other
wastes, to injure or interfere with any plants, create a public nuisance, or
create any hazard in the receiving waters or the wastewater treatment works,
including but not limited to, cyanide in excess of two milligrams per liter as
CN in the wastes as discharged to the public sewer.
      (3)   Any waters or wastes having a pH lower than 5.5 or having any other
corrosive property capable of causing damage or hazard to structures, equipment
and personnel of the wastewater treatment works.
      (4)   Solid or viscous substances in quantities or of such size capable
of causing obstruction to the flow in sewers or other interference with the
proper operation of the wastewater treatment works, such as but not limited to,
ashes, cinders, sand, mud, straw, shavings, metal, glass, rags, feathers, tar,
plastics, wood, un-ground garbage and paper dishes, cups, milk containers, and
the like, either whole or ground by garbage grinders.
      (5)   Any persistent pesticides or herbicides, such as dieldrin, aldrin,
chlordane, endrin, heptachlor, toxaphene, lindane and BAC, or other toxic
refractory organic chemicals.
   (D)   Maximum concentrations of heavy metals.
      (1)   Any liquid or wastes from nonresidential point source discharges to
the City's sewerage system shall not exceed the following concentrations for
the listed heavy metals, if attainable by the best practicable control
technology available:
Heavy Metal mg/l
Heavy Metal mg/l
Arsenic     0.05
Barium      5.0
Boron       1.0
Cadmium     0.02
Chromium    5.0
Copper      1.0
Lead        0.1
Manganese   1.0
Mercury     0.005
Nickel      1.0
Selenium    0.02
Silver      0.02
Zinc        5.0
 
      (2)   The dilution of the water or wastes of any nonresidential point
source, which would reduce the concentration of any such metals in the wastes
or waters discharged, does not constitute an acceptable manner of disposal.
      (3)   If the Federal Environmental Protection Agency develops heavy metal
limitations for a discharger into a publicly owned treatment works, the
limitations established in this division shall correspond to that revised
Environmental Protection Agency heavy metal limitation.
   (E)   Restricted discharges. No person shall discharge or cause to be
discharged the following described substances, water or wastes into the
sewerage system, which can harm the wastewater treatment works, can have an
adverse effect on the receiving stream, or can otherwise endanger life, limb or
public property or constitute a nuisance. The substances that must be
considered include, but are not limited to, the following:
      (1)   Any liquid or vapor having a temperature higher than 140°
Fahrenheit (or 60° Celsius) at the service connection to the City's system.
      (2)   Any water or waste containing fats, grease, wax or oils, whether
emulsified or not, in excess of 100 milligrams per liter, or containing
substances that may solidify or become viscous at temperatures between 32° and
140° Fahrenheit (0° and 60° Celsius).
      (3)   Any garbage that has not been properly shredded. The installation
and operation of any garbage grinder larger than those normally manufactured
and sold for residential and noncommercial use will not be permitted without
specific review and approval by the Water and Sewer Department.
      (4)   Any whole blood, paunch manure, hair, fleshing or entrails.
      (5)   Any waters or wastes containing strong acid, iron pickling wastes,
or concentrated lathing solutions; such wastes cannot be discharged into the
wastewater treatment works unless neutralized and approved for discharge by the
Water and Sewer Department.
      (6)   Any waters or wastes containing reducing substances of an organic
or inorganic nature, toxic or non-toxic, that exert an immediate chlorine
demand; such wastes cannot be discharged into the wastewater treatment works if
discharge of such agents will prevent the achievement of an adequate chlorine
residual in the effluent of the wastewater treatment works.
      (7)   Any waters or wastes containing phenols or other taste- or odor-
producing substances in concentrations exceeding limits established by the
Water and Sewer Department, after treatment of the composite sewage, to meet
the requirements of State, Federal or other public agencies having jurisdiction
over such discharge to the receiving waters.
      (8)   Any radioactive wastes or isotopes of such half-life or
concentration as may exceed limits established by the Water and Sewer
Department in compliance with applicable State and Federal regulations.
      (9)   Materials that cause or exert:
         (a)   Unusual concentrations of inert suspended solids (such as but
not limited to, fuller's earth, lime slurries and lime residues) or of
dissolved solids (such as, but not limited to, sodium chloride and sodium
sulfate).
         (b)   Unusual chemical oxygen demand or biochemical oxygen demand, or
chlorine requirements in such quantities as to constitute a significant load on
the wastewater treatment works.
         (c)   Excessive discoloration (such as, but not limited to, dye wastes
and vegetable tanning solutions).
         (d)   Slugs or shocks constituting an unusual volume of flow or
concentration of wastes, which will disturb the normal functioning of the
wastewater treatment works.
      (10)   Waters or wastes containing substances that are not amenable to
treatment or reduction employed by the wastewater treatment works, or that are
amenable to treatment only to such degree that the effluent cannot meet the
requirements of agencies having jurisdiction over discharge to the receiving
waters.
      (11)   Any water or waste discharge that, collectively with other
discharges, containing concentrations of heavy metals that cause the treated
effluent discharge from the City's wastewater treatment plant to exceed the
values listed in division (1) of this section.
         (a)   Maximum values are as follows:
Heavy Metal mg/l
Heavy Metal      mg/l
Arsenic          0.05
Barium           1.0
Boron            0.75
Cadmium          0.01
Chromium (total) 0.01

Manganese        0.01
Mercury          0.001
Molybdenum       0.01

Zinc             0.5
 
The concentration of heavy metals specified must not be interpreted to mean
that only dilution of heavy metal wastes constitutes an acceptable manner of
disposal. These heavy metals will be excluded or removed to the lowest degree
that is practicable.
         (b)   In determining whether the effluent of the City's plants is in
compliance with this division, the concentration of a heavy metal in the
background will be subtracted from the total concentration of that heavy metal
in the effluent.
         (c)   If the State Environmental Improvement Agency revises the
effluent limitation for chromium, the limitation for chromium established by
this division shall correspond to that revised State Environmental Improvement
Agency effluent limitation; except that in no case shall the concentration of
chromium in the effluent exceed 0.05 milligrams per liter.
         (d)   The limitations set out in division (11)(a) above shall in no
case exceed the following values for the listed heavy metals:
 
Heavy Metal mg/l
Arsenic     0.075
Cadmium     0.015
Lead        0.075
Mercury     0.0015
Copper      0.020
Silver      0.10
 
         (e)   If the Federal Environmental Protection Agency revises the heavy
metal limitations, the limitations established by this division shall
correspond to that revised Environmental Protection Agency heavy metal
limitation.
   (F)   Acceptance of restricted wastes. If any waters or wastes are
discharged or are proposed to be discharged into public sewers, and such waters
or wastes contain any of the substances or possess any of the characteristics
enumerated in division (E) of this section, and the discharge may have a
deleterious effect upon the wastewater treatment works or receiving waters, or
otherwise create a hazard to life or constitute a public nuisance, the Liquid
Waste Division may:
      (1)   Reject the waters;
      (2)   Require pretreatment to an acceptable condition for discharge into
public sewers; or
      (3)   Require control over the quantities and rates of discharge into the
public sewer system.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-7) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-
2007; Ord. 2009-05, passed 5-26-2009)
§ 51.08 GREASE, OIL AND SAND INTERCEPTORS.
   (A)   Grease, oil and sand interceptors shall be provided and properly
maintained by the owner when, in the opinion of the Building Inspection
Division or the Wastewater Department, they are necessary for the proper
handling of liquid wastes containing grease in excessive amounts, or any
flammable wastes, sand or other harmful ingredients.
   (B)   Grease, oil and sand interceptors are subject to the following
additional regulations:
      (1)   Such traps shall not be required for private living quarters or
dwelling units.
      (2)   All traps installed shall be sized as required by the International
Plumbing Code as adopted by the City.
      (3)   All traps shall be located so as to be readily and easily
accessible for cleaning and inspection. Inspections may be carried out on a
scheduled or a random basis.
      (4)   All traps shall be cleaned sufficiently often so as to prevent any
discharge of grease, oil or sand into the City sewer system, and the owner of
the premises shall keep records of the cleaning of all traps on the premises.
These records shall be available for inspection by an authorized representative
of the Building Inspection Division or Wastewater Department during normal
business hours.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-8) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-
2007; Ord. 2008-06, passed 11-24-2008) Penalty, see §
51.99

   The City shall, by ordinance, charge and collect from all users of sewer
lines and sewage system, for the use thereof, a monthly service charge. No free
service shall be provided for any user, public or private. The base rates for
sewer service are as follows:

                                       to June 30, 2011

Outside City Limits:                   $76.66

   (A)   The minimum (or base) monthly sewer charges shall be adjusted
annually, at the beginning of the fiscal year, starting July 1, 2012 using the
Consumer Price Index (CPI) as calculated and published by the State of New
Mexico.
   (B)   Commodity rate. Thereafter, a commodity rate shall be charge for each
additional 1,000 gallons for residential users as follows:
      Under 1,000      $0.00
      1,000 to 4,999      $0.25

      15,000 or more   $1.85

additional 1,000 gallons for all commercial accounts.
   (C)   Ruidoso Downs Race Track minimum monthly charge. To be repealed as is
covered under division (A) above.
   (D)   Sports Theater minimum monthly charge. To be repealed as is covered
under division (A) above.
   (E)   Sewer connections servicing multiple units. For the purpose of this
provision, UNIT is defined as part of the property, intended for, and shall be
charged as residential (including mobile home parks and apartment buildings),
commercial (including office complexes and malls), industrial or any type of
independent use, including one or more rooms or enclosed spaces
interconnecting, located on one or more floors in a building, and with a direct
exit to a public street or highway, or to a common area or mall leading to a
public street or highway, but shall not include nonresidential recreational
vehicles. Hotels, motels and nonresidential, tourist-related recreational
vehicle parks and those businesses required to pay Lodger's Tax, as per §§ 3-

shall be charged the minimum monthly charge for sewer service multiplied by the
number of units being serviced by the sewer connection. The regular commercial
sewer rate shall be charged per unit to commercial multiple units. In addition,
each sewer connection servicing more than one unit shall be charged the
commodity charge for that amount of liquid waste discharged that is in excess
of the number of units being served by the sewer connection multiplied by
1,000. Multiple units serviced by single meters shall be charged usage rates
based upon the number of units.
   (F)   Sewer System Capital Equipment and Infrastructure Fund.  A flat fee
shall be assessed on each sewer account to provide funds for the sole purpose
of providing a reserve fund for sewer system capital infrastructure and
equipment necessary to properly operate and maintain the sanitary sewer system.
This fee shall be $1.48 per month.
   (G)   Tank truck discharge. Tank truck discharge of liquid waste into the
City sewer system and the regional wastewater treatment plant interceptor line
is expressly prohibited.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007; Ord. 2011-02, passed 5-23-2011)
§ 51.10 SEWER BILLS.
   (A)   Sewer bills shall be prepared and posted on a cycle billing system,
whereby each user is billed each 30 days for service provided to such user in
the preceding 30-day period.
   (B)   Such amounts shall be due and payable on or before the tenth day after
billing, and failure to pay any such billing on or before the tenth day after
such billing shall result in any such account being delinquent.
   (C)   Failure to pay any delinquent account in full on or before the
twentieth day after billing shall be cause for the termination of water and
sewer service to any such customer, and the supply of water to any such
customer shall be forthwith terminated at the meter. Customers without water
service will have their sewer line plugged at their connection to the City
sewer main. A disconnect charge to cover time, materials, and incidentals will
be assessed to the customer's account to cover the cost of disconnect and
reconnect of not less than $300.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-10) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-
2007; Ord. 2011-02, passed 5-23-2011)

   The City shall have a lien on each lot or parcel of land connected with the
sewer system for charge made for services furnished by the system. Notice of
such lien shall be filed and such liens shall be enforced as provided by §§ 3-
36-1 et seq. NMSA 1978, as amended, and all other laws thereunto enabling.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-11) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-

§ 51.12 CONNECTION REQUIRED.
   (A)   All occupied property in the City used for human habitation or
occupancy, which is capable of being served by the public sewer system, shall
be connected with the public sewer system; and no person shall maintain, use or
operate a privy, cesspool or septic tank located on property that can be served
by the public sewer system; provided that no person shall be required to cross
the private property of any other person to make such sewer connections; and
provided further that. in lieu of public sewer connection where no public sewer
line is accessible, approved septic tank and seepage facilities shall be
installed.
   (B)   A written or printed notice to connect with the public sewer system
shall be given by order of the Governing Body to any owner or occupant of
property that is not connected with the system, but is capable of being served
by the public sewer system, and unless the time for connection be extended by
the Governing Body, all connections shall be made within 30 days after the
mailing of the required notice.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-12) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-

51.99
§ 51.13 CONNECTIONS OUTSIDE CITY.
   (A)   Water. The furnishing and supplying of water from the water system of
the City to any lot, piece or parcel of land located outside the corporate
limits of the City, or to any building, structure or improvement located
thereon, is expressly prohibited, unless expressly approved by the City
Council.
   (B)   Sewer connection. The connection to the sanitary sewer system of the
City with any sewer, pipe, line or connection serving any lot, piece or parcel
of land located outside the corporate limits, or serving any building,
structure or improvement located thereon, is expressly prohibited, unless
expressly approved by the City Council.
   (C)   Exceptions. Nothing contained in this section shall be construed to
prohibit or prevent the furnishing of water and/or sewer facilities to land,
buildings, structures and improvements located thereon outside the corporate
limits, which are used exclusively for educational, recreation, social,
athletic, agricultural, industrial, manufacturing or processing purposes.
   (D)   Violation by City officers and employees. All officers and employees
of the City are hereby forbidden to authorize or permit the connection of the
water and sewer systems of the City to any lands located outside the corporate
limits, or to any buildings, structures or improvements located thereon, unless
prior approval is obtained by the City Council.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007; Ord. 2010-07, passed 11-8-2010) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.14 MANDATORY CHARGES.
   For the purpose of maintaining, enlarging, constructing and repairing the

§ 51.15 SEWER AND WATER LINE INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Installation required. No land shall be connected to the sewer or
water system of the City until sewer and water lines have been installed as
required herein.
   (B)   Line size.  No land shall be connected to the sewer and water
facilities of the City until there are first installed water and sewer lines
within the full length of the street adjacent to the land, in the size required
by the City Engineer, but not less than a six-inch water main and an eight-inch
sewer main. The water and sewer facility shall be installed at the cost of the
owner, agent or occupant of land to be connected to the facilities.
      (1)   When land being connected to the water and sewer systems of the
City is required to be upgraded beyond the needs of the development, the
developer shall be reimbursed a pro rata share of the costs as determined by
the City, the terms and conditions of which shall have been mutually agreed to,
in writing, by both parties prior to authorization for construction. The cost
differential shall normally be identified by competitive bidding of the
extension, with and without the required upgrades. The reimbursement shall be
due upon City acceptance of the installed facilities, subject to the
availability of funds; in the event that funds are not available upon City
acceptance, the reimbursement may be prorated over a period not to exceed ten
years.
      (2)   For in-fill development only, where public utility line extensions
are required, water and sewer main line pipe only (valves, fittings, tapping
saddles, service line materials, fire hydrants, manholes and other such
appurtenances are specifically excluded) shall be furnished by the City at no
cost to the developer. Public utility extensions shall be required across the
entire frontage(s) of the subdivision or development. A partial extension shall
not be accepted.
      (3)   IN-FILL DEVELOPMENT shall be defined as those vacant parcel(s) of
land lying within the municipal boundaries that have been bypassed, remained
vacant or underused as a result of the continuing urban development process
immediately adjacent to the project. To be considered IN-FILL DEVELOPMENT, the
property must be located on an existing dedicated (improved or unimproved)
right-of-way, and have existing City water and/or sewer service to those
properties on both sides of and immediately adjacent to the development, and
fronting the right-of-way. Such development shall not apply to service lines to
individual customers.
   (C)   Compaction requirements. On all excavations within the City rights-of-
way, the contractor is required to use either “engineered” or “flowable” fill,
or prove, in writing (by a company licensed to perform compaction tests), a
minimum of 95% compaction on the filled excavation upon completion. A fee
assessment, as mentioned above, will be billed to the contractor or plumber if
City Hall is not provided with compaction proof within 14 days of excavation
closure.
   (D)   Construction specifications. Construction shall comply with New Mexico
Specifications for Public Works Construction, 1979 or later edition, prepared
by the New Mexico chapter of the American Public Works Administration. No
construction shall begin until the City Engineer has approved:
      (1)   Plans and specifications with an estimate of the cost of
construction; and
      (2)   Arrangements by the owner or contractor for inspection, testing and
final approval by a registered professional engineer.
   (E)   Offer to City; as-built plans.  Upon completion of any extension, it
shall be offered to the City free of encumbrances, with a copy of as-built
plans and the maintenance bond or warranty as required herein. If all
requirements are complied with, it shall be accepted for the City by the City
Public Works Director or City Engineer.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007)
§ 51.16 UNLAWFUL HABITATION.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to use, as a place of human habitation
public or private enterprise, any building within the City not equipped with
proper plumbing and having sewer or septic tank connections. It shall be
unlawful for the owner of any building used as a place of human habitation and
not having proper plumbing, and a sewer or septic tank connection, to allow the
same to be used as living quarters, or to rent the same for living purposes.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-14) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-
2007; Ord 2011-02, passed 5-23-2011) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.17 NUISANCES.
   All places of human habitation within the City not equipped with proper
plumbing and connected to sewer lines, or a septic tank, are hereby declared to
be nuisances and are prohibited, and all remedies for the abatement of such
nuisance may be used, and the penalties provided for in this chapter shall not
affect the right of the City to such remedies.
(1988 Code, § 4-4-15) (Ord. 88-3, passed 7-14-1988; Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-
2007) Penalty, see §
51.99
§ 51.99 PENALTY.
   Any person or business connecting to the sanitary sewer system of the City
contrary to and in violation of the terms of §§
51.04,
51.08,
51.12,
51.13,
51.16 and
51.17 of this chapter, or any officer or employee of the City authorizing,
permitting or in any way assisting the connection to the water and/or sewer
system of the City in violation hereof, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. Each
person or business found guilty or pleading “no contest” shall be subject to a
mandatory fine of $350 for the first offense, and thereafter, $500 for each
subsequent offense.
(Ord. 2007-04, passed 3-26-2007)

**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 52.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BUSINESS, COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENT, or INSTITUTION. Any building, structure,
or premises not defined as a "residence."
   COMMERCIAL GARBAGE. Any garbage produced by a business, commercial
establishment, or institution.
   GARBAGE. All putrescible wastes from kitchens, pantries, dining rooms, or
other parts of hotels, restaurants, boarding houses, tenement houses, dwelling
houses, markets, meat or poultry houses, factories, and any other place where
meats, fish, fowl, fruits, or vegetables are prepared for food for consumption,
and all household waste containing organic matter that has resulted from the
preparation of food, or other such worthless, offensive matter, the
accumulation of which may create a nuisance or be deleterious to public health
or offensive to sight or smell.
   GLASS PRODUCTS. Any product of a hard, brittle substance, usually
transparent.
   METAL PRODUCTS. Any of a class of chemical elements, such as iron, gold,
copper, and the like, that have luster and can conduct heat and electricity.
   PAPER PRODUCTS. Any product used to write or print on, wrap, and the like.
   PLASTIC PRODUCTS. Any product that can be molded or shaped, being any of
various non-metallic compounds, synthetically produced, which can be molded or
hardened.
   REFUSE. Non-putrescible solid waste such as waste paper, excelsior, rags,
wooden, cardboard, or paper boxes, bottles, broken ware, tin cans, metal
scraps, small mechanical parts, shavings, floor sweepings, and all other things
of a similar nature, but not including debris resulting from construction,
reconstruction, or repair of premises, fallen trees, tree limbs, yard
clippings, grass cuttings, yard cleanings, or other waste matter that is not
properly contained as hereinafter provided.
   RESIDENCE. Any building or structure used solely as a family domicile,
including single- or multiple-family dwelling units, apartments, rooming
houses, and boarding houses, but not including hotels, tourist cabins, motels,
motor courts, trailer courts, or apartment hotels.
   TRASH. All putrescible and non-putrescible solid waste, including garbage,
rubbish, dead animals, fallen trees, tree limbs, yard clippings, grass
cuttings, yard cleanings, and solid market and industrial wastes, but not
including debris resulting from construction, reconstruction, or repairs of
premises.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-1) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -)
§ 52.02 SUPERVISOR OF SANITATION DEPARTMENT.
   Any person designated by the Mayor and confirmed by the City Council as
Supervisor of the Sanitation Department shall have full charge and direction
over the Department and of all the employees therein.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-2) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -)
**** GARBAGE AND REFUSE DISPOSAL ****
§ 52.15 CONTAINERS FOR TRASH AND RECYCLABLES.
   (A)   Each owner, occupant, tenant, or lessee using or occupying any
building, house, structure, or grounds within the boundaries of the City shall
be provided watertight containers for garbage collection with tight-fitting
lids or covers and with handles sufficiently strong for workers to empty the
containers conveniently. All trash, garbage, and refuse must be drained of all
liquids and sacked or wrapped in durable paper or plastic before the garbage is
placed in the garbage containers.
   (B)   The City, by majority vote, may adopt a resolution requiring that all
metal products, paper products, glass products, and plastic products be
separated one from the other, so that the City may recycle these materials, or,
if the owner, occupant, tenant, or lessee desires to recycle them, he or she
may do so. These products shall be separated and packaged in durable paper or
plastic, unless the size of the object prohibits same.
   (C)   All trash, refuse, and garbage placed in containers must fit in the
containers. If it does not, special arrangements must be made with the
Supervisor of the Sanitation Department, by contacting the Supervisor. A charge
for the hauling of trash, garbage, and refuse which does not fit into the
containers provided shall be made by the City based upon its expense incurred
in the disposal thereof, including operational and capitalization expense.
   (D)   Garbage containers shall be maintained in a sanitary condition and
shall be thoroughly cleaned as needed. If damaged, the container will be
replaced and the owner, occupant, tenant, or lessee shall be assessed the
actual cost of the replacement by the City.
   (E)   All large refuse such as boxes, cartons, and crates shall be collapsed
before being placed in containers. Ashes shall not be placed in any receptacle.
Debris resulting from the construction, reconstruction, or repairs of premises
shall not be placed with other trash for collection, but shall be disposed of
directly by the workers or person or persons owning, occupying, or leasing the
premises wherein that debris is accumulated. Special arrangements may be made
with the Supervisor of the Sanitation Department for the disposal thereof, but
any costs incurred by the City shall be passed directly on to the owner of the
garbage, trash, or refuse.
   (F)   No person shall dump or deposit, or cause to be dumped or deposited
any garbage in boxes or bins designated for refuse, including paper, glass, or
metal containers which have been saturated with or still contain organic wastes
that may attract insects or rodents or generate noxious or offensive gases or
odors, or any dead animal. No person shall dump or deposit, or cause to be
dumped or deposited any ashes in boxes or bins designated for refuse.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-3) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.16 LIDS AND COVERS OF TRASH CONTAINERS.
   The lids or covers of containers shall at all times be kept secure so that
flies and other insects may not have access to the contents thereof. The lids
or covers shall only be removed while the containers and receptacles are being
filled, emptied, or cleaned.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-4) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.17 PLACEMENT OF GARBAGE CONTAINERS.
   Receptacles or containers of the type used for garbage or residential refuse
shall be kept in a place convenient to and easily accessible for the collection
thereof.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-5) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.18 PLACEMENT OF REFUSE BINS.
   Bins of the type used for storage or refuse shall be placed as follows.
   (A)   Refuse bins maintained for one premises shall be located on the same
side of the alley, except that the City Clerk/Treasurer may temporarily waive
this requirement in extreme hardship cases.
   (B)   No refuse bin shall be placed beneath a fire escape or so as to
restrict passage from an exit door. No refuse bins shall be placed under a
street floor window unless the window is of fire resistant construction and the
window is not needed to meet ventilation requirements of the building.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-6) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -)
§ 52.19 INSPECTION OF GARBAGE AND REFUSE RECEPTACLES.
   (A)   The City Clerk/Treasurer shall require regular inspections to secure
compliance with §§
52.15 through
52.23 of this Code with reference to receptacles for garbage and refuse. The
City Clerk/Treasurer shall notify the owners or occupants of the property upon
which violations occur. The City Clerk/Treasurer and the Supervisor of the
Sanitation Department shall, within regular business hours, have the power to
enter commercial and business establishments for inspection purposes.
   (B)   These provisions for inspection shall in no way limit the right of
representatives of the State or local Health Department or representatives of
the Building or Fire Departments from inspecting.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-7) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.20 DEPOSIT OF GARBAGE OR REFUSE OTHER THAN IN AUTHORIZED CONTAINERS
PROHIBITED.
   The owner, occupant, tenant, or lessee of any premises within the City shall
be responsible for the sanitary conditions of the premises occupied by him or
her, and no person shall keep in or about any premises occupied by him or her
any garbage or refuse as herein defined unless the same is kept in authorized
containers, nor shall any person bury, dump, or deposit or cause to be buried,
dumped, or deposited upon any street or alley or premises any garbage, trash,
or refuse of any kind whatsoever.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-8) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.21 BURNING OF REFUSE RESTRICTED.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to set fire or to cause or procure
a fire to be set to any trash, refuse, inflammable vegetation, or forest
material, or to any other flammable substance on his or her own land or that of
another person.
   (B)   Special permits may be considered by the City Council at regularly
scheduled meetings.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-9) (Ord. 94-08, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.22 HAULING OF GARBAGE OR REFUSE.
   (A)   No person shall haul or cause to be hauled, on or along any public
street or alley in the City, any garbage or refuse unless those materials shall
be contained in vehicles or receptacles so constructed as to prevent the
contents from falling, leaking, blowing, or spilling therefrom, or any odor
escaping therefrom, and to prevent any flies, insects, or rodents from having
access to the contents thereof. These vehicles or receptacles shall be
constructed and maintained in a manner prescribed by the City Clerk/Treasurer.
   (B)   Every person hauling any refuse along the streets or alleys of the
City shall replace immediately in the conveyance used for the hauling thereof,
any contents which may fall therefrom in or upon any street, alley, or premises
within the limits of the City.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-10) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.23 SCAVENGING; TAMPERING WITH CONTAINERS.
   No person, unless authorized by the owner of a trash container, shall remove
the lid from that trash container in order to remove, collect, or disturb the
trash stored in the container. No person shall remove any trash from a
container and scatter the same upon a public alley, street, or sidewalk. No
person shall tip over or scatter any trash or garbage.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-11) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.24 MEDICAL WASTE.
   No person shall deposit any medical waste, including hypodermic needles or
syringes, in any container that is accessible to children.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-12) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.25 THROWING AND DRAINING TRASH INTO WATERS AND DITCHES PROHIBITED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to drain any water, slop, or other
substance whatsoever, or to throw cans, wire, broken glassware, crockery,
bottles, bones, weeds, rubbish, cast-off clothing, shoes, paper, dead animals,
or any other filth or trash of any kind whatsoever into the rivers, streams, or
bar ditches within the City.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-13) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.26 UNLAWFUL DISPOSAL OF REFUSE.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to discard refuse:
      (1)   On public property in any manner other than by placing the refuse
in a receptacle provided for that purpose by any responsible government
authority, or otherwise in accordance with lawful directions; or
      (2)   On private property not owned or lawfully occupied or controlled by
the person, except with the consent of the owner, lessee, or occupant thereof.
   (B)   The use of Uniform Traffic Citations are authorized for the
enforcement of this chapter.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-14) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.27 FEE FOR GARBAGE DISPOSAL; RESPONSIBILITY.
   Each owner, lessee, tenant, or occupant of any premises where garbage,
refuse, and trash are created or accumulated and each resident in the City
shall pay the City for collection of garbage, refuse, and trash.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-15) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §

**** DANGEROUS BUILDINGS OR PREMISES ****
§ 52.40 NOTICE TO REMOVE; OBJECTION.
   (A)   Whenever any building or structure is ruined, damaged, and
dilapidated, or any premises is covered with ruins, rubbish, wreckage, or
debris, the Governing Body of the City may, by resolution, find that the
ruined, damaged, and dilapidated building, structure, or premises is a menace
to the public comfort, health, peace, or safety and require the removal from
the Municipality of the building, structure, ruins, rubbish, wreckage, or
debris.
   (B)   A copy of the resolution shall be served on the owner, occupant, or
agent in charge of the building, structure, or premises. If the owner (as shown
by the real estate records of the County Clerk), occupant, or agent in charge
of the building, structure, or premises cannot be served within the
Municipality, a copy of the resolution shall be posted on the building,
structure, or premises and a copy of the resolution shall be published one
time.
   (C)   Within ten days of the receipt of a copy of the resolution or of the
posting and publishing of a copy of the resolution, the owner, occupant, or
agent in charge of the building, structure, or premises shall commence removing
the building, structure, ruin, rubbish, wreckage, or debris, or file a written
objection with the City Clerk/Treasurer, asking for a hearing before the
Governing Body of the Municipality.
   (D)   If a written objection is filed as required in this section, the
Governing Body shall:
      (1)   Fix a date for a hearing on its resolution and the objection;
      (2)   Consider all evidence for and against the removal resolution at the
hearing; and
      (3)   Determine if its resolution should be enforced or rescinded.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-17) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.41 APPEAL.
   (A)   Any person aggrieved by the determination of the Governing Body of the
City may appeal to the District Court by:
      (1)   Giving notice of appeal to the Governing Body of the City within
five days after the determination made by the Governing Body of the City; and
      (2)   Filing a petition in the District Court within 20 days after the
determination made by the Governing Body of the City.
   (B)   The District Court shall hear the matter de novo and enter judgment in
accordance with its findings.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-17) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -)
§ 52.42 REMOVAL BY CITY; RECOVERY OF COSTS.
   (A)   If the owner, occupant, or agent in charge of the building, structure,
or premises fails to commence removing the building, structure, ruin, rubbish,
wreckage, or debris within the following time periods, the Municipality may
remove the building, structure, ruins, rubbish, wreckage, or debris at the cost
and expense of the owner:
      (1)   Within ten days of being served a copy of the resolution or of the
posting and publishing of the resolution;
      (2)   Within five days of the determination by the Governing Body of the
City that the resolution shall be enforced; or
      (3)   After the District Court enters judgment sustaining the
determination of the Governing Body of the City.
   (B)   The reasonable cost of the removal shall constitute a lien against the
building, structure, ruin, rubbish, wreckage, or debris so removed and against
the lot or parcel of land from which it was removed. The lien shall be
foreclosed in the manner provided in §§ 3-36-1 through 3-36-6 NMSA 1978.
   (C)   The Municipality may pay for the costs of removal of any condemned
building, structure, wreckage, rubbish, or debris by granting to the person
removing the materials the legal title to all salvageable materials in lieu of
other compensation.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-17) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -)
§ 52.43 REMOVAL; RESTORATION TO SAFE CONDITION REQUIRED.
   Any person or firm removing any condemned building, structure, wreckage,
rubbish, or debris shall leave the premises from which the material has been
removed in a clean, level, and safe condition, suitable for further occupancy
or construction, and with all excavations filled.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-17) (Ord. 90-03, passed - -) Penalty, see §
52.99
§ 52.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who shall violate any provision of this chapter for which
no other penalty is provided shall be subject to penalties as provided in §
10.99 of this Code.
   (B)   (1)   The City may enforce obedience to this chapter by imposing, for
any violation thereof, a fine not exceeding $500, or by imprisonment not
exceeding 90 days, or by both such a fine and imprisonment, by suit or
prosecution before the Municipal Judge of the Municipality.
      (2)   Each violation shall be a separate offense. Should a violation
occur for more than one day, for each day that it occurs, it shall be deemed a
separate offense.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-18)
   (C)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
52.21 of this Code shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction
thereof shall be fined in an amount not to exceed $300 or be imprisoned in the
County Jail for a period not to exceed 90 days, or be both so fined and
imprisoned. Each day such a violation is committed or permitted to continue
shall constitute a separate offense and shall be punishable as such hereunder.
(1988 Code, § 4-7-9)
(Ord. 90-03, passed - -; Ord. 93-12, passed - -; Ord. 94-08, passed - -)

   (B)   The term PENALTY ASSESSMENT MISDEMEANOR does not include any violation
that has caused or contributed to the cause of an accident resulting in injury
or death to any person.
   (C)   When an alleged violator of a penalty assessment misdemeanor elects to
accept a notice to appear in lieu of notice of penalty assessment, no fine
later imposed upon conviction shall exceed the penalty assessment established
for the particular penalty assessment misdemeanor, and no probation imposed
upon a suspended or deferred sentence shall exceed 90 days.
   (D)   The penalty assessment for speeding in violation of § 12-6-1.2(4) of
the Uniform Traffic Ordinance is twice the penalty assessment established in
division (A) of this section for the equivalent miles per hour over the speed
limit.
(Ord. 2009-11, passed 10-26-2009; Ord. 2013-01, passed 2-11-2013; Ord. 2014-02,
passed 7-14-2014; Ord. 2019-02, passed 10-15-2019; Ord. 2024-01, passed 8-26-
2024)
§ 70.03 PENALTY ASSESSMENT MISDEMEANORS; OPTION; EFFECT.
   (A)   Unless a warning notice is given, at the time of making an arrest for
any penalty assessment misdemeanor, the arresting officer shall offer the
alleged violator the option of accepting a penalty assessment. The violator's
signature on the penalty assessment notice constitutes an acknowledgement of
guilt of the offense stated in the notice, and payment of the prescribed
penalty assessment is a complete satisfaction of the violation.
   (B)   Payment of any penalty assessment must be made by mail to the
Municipal Court, Traffic Violations Bureau, City of Ruidoso Downs, New Mexico,
within 15 days from the date of arrest. (Ord. 2009-11, passed 10-26-2009; Ord.
2019-02, passed 10- 15-2019)
§ 70.04 FAILURE TO PAY PENALTY ASSESSMENT.
   (A)   If a penalty assessment is not paid within 15 days from the date of
arrest, the violator shall be prosecuted for the violation charged on the
penalty assessment notice in a manner as if the penalty assessment notice had
not been issued. Upon conviction in such prosecution, the court shall impose
penalties as provided by the New Mexico Uniform Traffic Ordinance (§ 12-12-
1.1), or other law relating to motor vehicles for the particular offense
charged, and the scheduled penalty assessments shall not apply.
   (B)   In addition to the prosecution provided for in division (A), it is a
misdemeanor for any person who has elected to pay a penalty assessment to fail
to do so within 15 days from the date of arrest.
   (C)   The Office of the Municipal Court shall notify the Motor Vehicle
Division of the State of New Mexico when a person fails to pay a penalty
assessment within the required period of time. The Motor Vehicle Division shall
report the notice upon the driver's record, and shall not renew the person's
license to drive until the Municipal Court notifies the Motor Vehicle Division
that the penalty assessment, or its equivalent, as well as any additional
penalties imposed, are properly disposed of.
(Ord. 2009-11, passed 10-26-2009; Ord. 2019-02, passed 10-15-2019)
