**** PARKS REGULATIONS ****
§ 93.01 PARKS ESTABLISHED.
   The All American Municipal Park, River Side Park and Heights Park situated
within the City, as set forth upon the plats thereof on file in the Office of
the City Clerk/Treasurer, shall be known as “the Parks.”
(1988 Code, § 4-5-1) (Ord. 2012-05, passed 8-27-2012; Ord. 2014-01, passed 7-
14-2014)
§ 93.02 USE AND CONDUCT REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Disorderly conduct as defined in §
131.17 of this Code, or any other use of the area in such a manner as to
unreasonably interfere with the use of the Park by others, is prohibited.
   (B)   The consumption of alcoholic beverages is prohibited in the Park, save
and except for special activities authorized from time to time by the Governing
Body and for which a picnic license has been obtained from the Department of
Alcoholic Beverage Control.
   (C)   All refuse shall be deposited in the designated containers.
   (D)   No commercial activities of any kind or nature shall be permitted in
the Park except for special activities authorized from time to time by the
Governing Body, and when so authorized, subject to the occupation license or
other tax requirements then in force in the City.
   (E)   Camp fires and cooking with the use of wood or charcoal are prohibited
except in designated fireplaces. Cooking is permitted in other areas with self-
contained portable units using butane, propane, or any liquid hydrocarbon
mixture.
   (F)   Under no circumstances shall overnight camping, whether in bedrolls,
tents, or recreational vehicles, be permitted.
   (G)   Park hours of operation shall be between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. daily
except for scheduled special events or tournaments approved by the City
Council.
(1988 Code, § 4-5-2) (Ord. 2012-05, passed 8-27-2012) Penalty, see §
93.99

**** EXCAVATIONS ****
§ 94.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ADVANCE NOTICE. Two working days.
   BLASTING. The use of an explosive to excavate.
   CABLE TELEVISION LINES AND RELATED FACILITIES. Facilities of any cable
television system or closed-circuit coaxial cable communications system or
other similar transmission service used in connection with any cable television
system or other similar closed-circuit coaxial cable communications system.
   COMMISSION. The State Corporation Commission or its successor agency.
   EMERGENCY. Any situation necessitating excavation for the purposes of
locating trouble or making repairs in a facility for the immediate protection
of life, property, or the public welfare.
   EXCAVATE. The movement or removal of earth using mechanical excavating
equipment or blasting; and includes augering, backfilling, digging, ditching,
drilling, grading, plowing in, pulling in, ripping, scraping, trenching, and
tunneling.
   EXCAVATOR. Any person required by this subchapter to give advance notice of
excavation.
   FACILITY. Any pipe, pipeline, tube, main service, manhole, meter, regulator,
valve, conduit, cable, or object of any kind or character, whether enumerated
in this definition or not, which is or may be lawfully constructed, left,
placed, or maintained in, upon, along, across, or under any public property or
private easements appearing of record or acquired by adverse possession or
prescriptive use.
   FILL. Placement of dirt or fill material of 50 yards or more on utility
easements in the City.
   MEANS OF LOCATION. A mark such as a stake in earthen areas or a point mark
in paved areas that is conspicuous in nature and that is designed to last at
least five days if not disturbed.
   MECHANICAL EXCAVATING EQUIPMENT. All equipment powered by any motor, engine,
or hydraulic or pneumatic device used for excavating; and includes trenchers,
bulldozers, backhoes, power shovels, scrapers, draglines, clam shells, augers,
drills, cable and pipe plows, or other plowing-in or pulling-in equipment.
   ONE-CALL NOTIFICATION SYSTEM. A communication system in which an operation
center provides telephone service or other reliable means of communication for
the purpose of receiving excavation notice information and distributing that
information to owners and operators of pipeline facilities.
   PERSON. The legal representative of or any individual, partnership,
corporation, joint venture, State, subdivision or instrumentality of the State,
or an association.
   PIPELINE. A pipeline or system of pipelines and appurtenances for the
transportation or movement of any oil or gas, or oil or gas products and by-
products; but not including gathering lines or systems operated exclusively for
the gathering of oil or gas, oil or gas products, and their by-products in any
field or area, lines or systems constituting a part of any tank farm, plant
facilities of any processing plant, or underground storage projects, unless it
is  located within a Municipality or in the boundaries of an established
easement or right-of-way or within the limits of any unincorporated city, town,
or village, or within any designated residential or commercial area such as a
subdivision, business or shopping center, or community development.
   UNDERGROUND FACILITIES. Any tangible property described in the definitions
of FACILITY  and UNDERGROUND UTILITY LINE which is underground and does not
include residential sprinklers or low-voltage lighting.
   UNDERGROUND UTILITY LINE. An underground conduit or cable, including fiber
optics, and related facilities for transportation and delivery of electricity,
telephonic or telegraphic communications, or water.
   UTILITY. Any person furnishing the public gas, water, electricity, sewer
service, telephone service, cable television, or a similar product or service.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -)
§ 94.02 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person, corporation, partnership, other
entity, or utility franchise to tunnel under or to make any excavation in any
street, alley, or other compacted traveling surface within the limits of the
City without having obtained a permit and paying the permit and restoration fee
as required in this subchapter, or without complying with the provisions of
this subchapter, or in violation of or variance from the terms of any such
permit.
   (B)   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definition shall
apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      STREET, ALLEY, OR OTHER COMPACTED TRAVELING SURFACE. Any paved or unpaved
all-weather surface, including, but not limited to, chip seal, hot mix asphalt,
cold mill asphalt, and base course.
   (C)   Public utilities which pay the City a franchise fee will be required
to acquire a permit for excavation in accordance with this subchapter without
the payment of a permit fee, with the payment of the applicable restoration
fee.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.03 PERMIT APPLICATION.
   Applications for the permit required by this subchapter shall be made to the
City, and shall describe the location of the intended excavation, tunnel, or
disturbance, the size thereof, the purpose thereof, the person or utility
franchise doing the actual excavation work, and the name of the person or
utility franchise for whom or which the work is being done. The permit shall
contain the agreement of the applicant that he or she will comply with all
ordinances and laws relating to the work to be done.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.04 PERMIT FEES.
   (A)   Fees set by Council. The fee for the permit required by this
subchapter shall be set by resolution of the City Council from time to time and
shall be then listed in a fee schedule attached to the current Excavations
Ordinance as Appendix A.
   (B)   Payment; purpose. No permit shall be issued unless the applicant
therefor has first applied to the City and payment has been made in the full
amount of the permit fee and restoration fee based on the footage of the cut to
be made, unless prior arrangements have been made with the City management. It
is the intention of the Council that the fee for these permits shall be for the
purpose of reimbursing the City for the costs incurred by the City in
performing the necessary permitting, inspections, and tests, and repairing the
surface of the cut made with pavement, chip seal, or base course as the case
may be. Therefore, the Council from time to time may, by resolution, raise or
lower the fee for these permits.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -)
§ 94.05 AGREEMENT TO LIABILITY FOR DAMAGES.
   (A)   No permit shall be issued under this subchapter by the City until the
applicant for the permit agrees to be and becomes responsible for any and all
damages that may ensue to the person or property of another or that may be
occasioned to the person or property of another by reason of the excavation,
tearing up, removing, or digging up any of the street, alley, or other
compacted traveling surface, and also agrees to indemnify, save, and hold
harmless the City by reason thereof. The issuance of the permit and payment of
the fee as set forth in this subchapter shall constitute the agreement to the
liability for damages of the person applying for the permit.
   (B)   All public utility companies who pay a franchise fee to the City may
satisfy the requirements of division (A) above by providing the City with proof
of liability insurance that lists the City as an additional insured.
   (C)   If any underground facility is damaged by any person who failed to
make reasonable efforts to inform himself or herself as to its location as
provided in Ch. 62, Art. 14 NMSA 1978, that person shall reimburse the owner of
the underground facility for the actual cost of damage to the underground
facility, including the cost of restoration of services. The person engaging in
the excavation may also be liable to the owner or operator of the underground
facility for the comparative negligence of the person engaging in the
excavation which results in damage to the facility, for an additional amount
not to exceed $500 for each occurrence.
   (D)   If any underground facility is damaged by any person who has made
reasonable efforts to inform himself or herself as to its location and the
damaged underground facility was correctly located by the owner or operator of
the underground facility as provided in § 62-14-5 NMSA 1978, then that person
causing the damage shall be liable to the owner or operator of the underground
facility for only the actual cost of damage to the underground facility,
including the cost of restoration of service.
   (E)   It is not the intent of Ch. 62, Art. 14 NMSA 1978 to impose civil
liability to any person beyond that provided in this section.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -)
§ 94.06 MANNER OF EXCAVATION.
   (A)   All pavement or chip seal cuts shall be made with a mechanical paving
or cement cutting device in order that all cuts may be straight and uniform in
nature. Proper bracing shall be maintained to prevent the collapse of adjoining
ground. In excavations, the excavation shall not have, anywhere below the
surface, any portion of the excavation which is wider than or which extends
beyond the opening or cut at the surface.
   (B)   Care should be taken so that no injury shall be done to any pipes,
cables, or conduits in the making of such excavations or tunnels. Notice should
be given to the persons maintaining any such pipes, cables, or conduits, or to
the City departments which are or may be endangered or affected by the making
of any such excavation or tunnel, 48 hours before the pipes, cables, or
conduits shall be disturbed, through the utility one-call system or through
cooperation with the utility council. No unnecessary damage or injury shall be
done to any tree or shrub or the roots thereof.
   (C)   All material excavated from the street cut shall be maintained on-site
so as to not interfere with traffic control, until such time that it is reused
in the backfill or hauled away. Any material which is excavated from a street
cut and is noticeably wet or otherwise unsuitable for backfill, as determined
by the Street Department, shall be disposed of, and proper backfill shall be
brought in at the applicant's expense.
   (D)   Every person who prepares engineering plans for excavation or who
engages in excavation shall:
      (1)   Make reasonable efforts to inform himself of the location of any
underground facility in or near the area where the excavation is to be
conducted, including a request to the owner or operator of the underground
facility to locate the underground facility pursuant to § 62-14-5 NMSA 1978;
      (2)   Plan the excavation to avoid or minimize interference or damage to
underground facilities in or near the excavation area;
      (3)   Provide reasonable (24 hours) advanced notice of the commencement,
extent, and duration of the excavation work to the owners of any existing
underground facility in and near the excavation area in order to allow the
owners to locate and mark the location of the underground facility described in
§ 62-14-5 NMSA 1978 prior to the commencement of work in the excavation area;
      (4)   Prior to initial exposure of the underground facility, maintain at
least an estimated clearance of 18 inches between existing underground
facilities for which the owners or operators have previously identified the
location, and the cutting edge or point of any mechanical excavating equipment
utilized in the excavation;
      (5)   Provide such support for existing underground facilities in or near
the excavation area as may be reasonably necessary to prevent damage to them;
      (6)   Backfill all excavations in a manner and with materials as may be
necessary to prevent damage to and provide reliable support during and
following backfilling for pre-existing underground facilities in or near the
excavation area; and
      (7)   Notify as promptly as possible the owner of any underground
facilities which may have been damaged or dislocated during the excavation
work.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.07 EXCAVATING IN STATE RIGHTS-OF-WAY.
   The City does not have jurisdiction for excavation and tunneling in the
State rights-of-way. Except in emergency situations, all permits and traffic
control will be required to have State Highway and Transportation Department
approval prior to any excavations or tunneling, unless other arrangements have
been made.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.08 EMERGENCY EXCAVATION.
   (A)   Every person who engages in emergency excavation shall take all
necessary and reasonable precautions to avoid or minimize interference with or
damage to existing underground facilities in and near the construction area and
shall notify as promptly as possible the owners of underground facilities
located in and near the emergency excavation area. In the event of any damage
to or dislocation of any underground facility caused by the emergency
excavation work, the person responsible for the excavation shall immediately
notify the owner of the underground facility.
   (B)   In those instances where it is not feasible or where it is physically
impossible to secure the proper permits due to emergencies at night, on
weekends, or on holidays, the party making the excavation will secure the
permit on the next working day after the work has been done. All emergency cuts
shall otherwise conform to the requirements of this subchapter.
   (C)   In some instances, where it will not be feasible or where it is
physically impossible to properly compact backfill to the requirements
contained in §
94.10 of this Code, the applicant may, upon the Street Department's approval,
fill in or cover up the excavation without compaction efforts. Once the Street
Department has determined the emergency situation is over, or when it is
feasible, the applicant will excavate down to the area in the excavation which
was previously compacted, prior to his or her excavation, and shall then comply
with the backfill requirements set forth in §
94.10.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.09 WARNING DEVICES AND BARRICADES; TRAFFIC CONTROL.
   (A)   It shall be the obligation of the applicant, employees, or agents, or
of the owner of the premises to be served, to place proper warning devices,
lights, barricades, and such signals and other devices on or near the
excavation in order that the public may be protected; and any person or utility
franchise who undertakes to excavate any street, alley, or public right-of-way
does so at his or her own risk.
   (B)   If any arterials or major or minor collectors are to be cut, and
traffic flow interrupted, a detailed plan for traffic control shall be
submitted at the time of application for the permit. All traffic-control
schemes and devices shall be in accordance with the latest edition of the
Manual of Uniform Traffic-Control Devices.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.10 BACKFILL.
   (A)   Material taken from a street cut may be reused as backfill, provided
it meets the requirements of the Street Department. If that material has been
deemed unsuitable, the applicant for the permit shall provide a base course or
other gravel type of bedding as backfill. The applicant is required to use
mechanical or vibratory compaction equipment necessary to compact a six-inch
layer of any backfill material to 95% of a modified proctor, with moisture
content at plus or minus 2% of the optimum moisture. It will be the option of
the Street Department to order compaction tests on any street cut backfill as
necessary, to ensure that there is no future soil settlement. The costs of this
testing shall be borne by the applicant.
   (B)   All fill over 50 cubic yards placed on utility lines and easements
must be permitted through the City.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.11 RESTORATION OF SURFACE.
   (A)   After any person or utility franchise making any excavation or tunnel
in or under any public street, alley, or other public right-of-way in the City
has completed the work for which the cut was made, he or she shall immediately
advise the City that the cut is ready for restoration, whereupon it shall be
the obligation of the Street Department of the City to restore the surface to
its original condition.
   (B)   For any cuts outside the paved surface, the contractor or utility
company shall take every effort and care to compact and restore the ground to
its original condition, to include compaction, grading, keeping drainage
structures clear, restoration of trees, or as required by the Street Department
Director. The Street Department will issue and the contractor will remedy or be
subject to citation, fine, or suspension of any permits issued to him or her.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.12 WARRANTY PERIOD.
   The person or utility franchise making any excavation in a public street,
alley, or other public right-of-way shall warrant his or her work for a period
of one year after completion. If settlement of a street cut or excavation
appears within a year, the person or utility franchise shall re-excavate the
site down to the utility or structure, and re-compact the site as set forth in
§
94.10 of this Code. The applicant will be required to apply for permits and pay
necessary fees as if this were the first application.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.13 ONE-CALL NOTIFICATION SYSTEM.
   (A)   Every owner, City, or operator of a pipeline facility within the City
shall be a member of a one-call notification system. A one-call notification
system may be for a region of the State or statewide in scope, unless Federal
law provides otherwise.
   (B)   Each one-call notification system shall be operated by:
      (1)   An owner or operator of pipeline facilities;
      (2)   A private contractor;
      (3)   A State or local government agency; or
      (4)   A person who is otherwise eligible under State law to operate a
one-call notification system.
   (C)   If the one-call notification system is operated by owners or operators
of pipeline facilities, it shall be established as a non-profit entity governed
by a board of directors that shall establish the operating processes,
procedures, and technology needed for a one-call notification system. The board
shall further establish a procedure or formula to determine the equitable share
of each member for the costs of the one-call notification system. The board may
include representatives of excavators or other persons deemed eligible to
participate in the system who are not owners or operators.
   (D)   Excavators shall give advance notice to the one-call notification
system operating in the intended excavation area and provide information
established by rule and regulation of the Commission, except when excavations
are by or for a person that:
      (1)   Owns or leases or owns a mineral leasehold interest in the real
property on which the excavation occurs; and
      (2)   Operates all underground facilities located in the intended
excavation area.
   (E)   The one-call notification system shall promptly transmit excavation
notice information to owners or operators of pipeline facilities in the
intended excavation area.
   (F)   After receiving advance notice, owners and operators of pipeline
facilities shall locate and mark their pipeline facilities in the intended
excavation area within 24-hour period work days.
   (G)   The one-call notification system shall provide a toll-free telephone
number or another comparable and reliable means of communication to receive
advance notice of excavation. Means of communication to distribute excavation
notice to owners or operators of pipeline facilities shall be reliable and
capable of coordination with one-call notification systems operating in other
regions of the State.
   (H)   Operators of a one-call notification system shall notify the
Commission of its members and the name and telephone number of the contact
person for each member.
   (I)   One-call notifications systems and owners and operators of pipeline
facilities shall promote public awareness of the availability and operation of
one-call notification systems and work with State and local governmental
agencies charged with issuing excavation permits to provide information
concerning, and promote awareness by excavators of the one-call notification
system.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.14 MARKING OF FACILITIES.
   (A)   Every person owning or operating an underground facility shall, upon
the request of a person intending to commence an excavation and upon reasonable
advance notice, locate and mark on the surface the actual horizontal location
within 18 inches by some means of locating the underground facilities in or
near the area of the excavation so as to enable the person engaged in
excavation work to locate the facilities in advance of and during the
excavation work.
   (B)   If the owner or operator fails to correctly mark the underground
facility after being given reasonable advance notice, and this failure to
correctly mark the facility results in additional cost to the person doing the
excavating, then the owner or operator shall reimburse the person engaging in
the excavation for the reasonable costs incurred or owner to fix repair or
repair at owner's expense.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -) Penalty, see §
94.99
§ 94.15 INSPECTIONS.
   The department head of the Street Department, or his or her authorized
representative, shall inspect or cause to be inspected all excavations and
tunnels being made in or under any public street, alley, or any other public
right-of-way in the City to see the enforcement of this subchapter.
(Ord. 2000-01, passed - -)

CHAPTER 95: STORMWATER POLLUTION PREVENTION: PHOSPHORUS ESTABLISHING
REGULATIONS
Section

95.05   Regulation of the use and application of lawn fertilizer

§ 95.01 AUTHORITY.
   The authority is as per §§ 3-12-2, 3-12-3, 3-17-1, 74-6-1 through 74-6-17
NMSA 1978 and as per 40 C.F.R. pts 402–403.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.02 PURPOSE AND INTENT.
   The City Council finds that the Rio Ruidoso is a natural asset, which
enhances the environmental, recreational, cultural and economic resources of
the area and contributes to the general health and welfare of the public. The
City Council further finds that regulating the amount of nutrients and
contaminants, including phosphorus contained in fertilizer, entering the river
will improve and maintain lake water quality.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.03 APPLICABILITY.
   This chapter applies in all areas within the corporate limits of the City of
Ruidoso Downs.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.04 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AGRICULTURAL USE. Has the meaning set forth in § 47-9-5A NMSA 1978 for
agricultural facility.
   FERTILIZER. Has the meaning set forth in § 76-11-3D. and E. NMSA 1978.
   LAWN FERTILIZER. Any fertilizer, whether distributed by property owner,
renter or commercial entity, distributed for nonagricultural use, such as for
lawns, golf courses, parks and cemeteries. LAWN FERTILIZER does not include
fertilizer products intended primarily for garden and indoor plant application.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.05 REGULATION OF THE USE AND APPLICATION OF LAWN FERTILIZER.
   (A)   Effective September 1, 2006, no person shall apply any lawn fertilizer
within City that is labeled as containing more than 0% phosphorus or other
compound containing phosphorus, such as phosphate, except as provided in §
95.06.
   (B)   No lawn fertilizer shall be applied when the ground is frozen or
covered with snow.
   (C)   No person shall apply fertilizer to any impervious surface including
parking lots, roadways, and sidewalks. If such application occurs, the
fertilizer must be immediately contained and either legally applied to turf or
placed in an appropriate container.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.06 EXEMPTIONS.
   The prohibition against the use of fertilizer under §
95.05 shall not apply to:
   (A)   Newly established turf or lawn areas during their first growing
season.
   (B)   Turf or lawn areas that soil tests, performed within the past three
years by a state approved (NMED or NMDA) soil testing laboratory, confirm are
below required phosphorus levels for lawns as established by the NMSU Extension
Service. The lawn fertilizer application shall not contain an amount of
phosphorus exceeding the amount and rate of application recommended in the soil
test evaluation.
   (C)   Agricultural uses, vegetable and flower gardens, or application to
trees or shrubs.
   (D)   Yard waste compost, biosolids (if treated to meet "class A" under 40
C.F.R. pt 503) or other similar materials that are primarily organic in nature
and are applied to improve the physical condition of the soil.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.07 SALE OF FERTILIZER CONTAINING PHOSPHORUS.
   (A)   Effective November 1, 2006, no person shall sell or offer for sale any
lawn fertilizer within City that is labeled as containing more than 0%
phosphorus, or other compound containing phosphorus, such as phosphate, except
such fertilizer may be sold for use as provided in §
95.06.
   (B)   Effective November 1, 2006, no person shall display lawn fertilizer
containing phosphorus. Signs may be posted advising customers that lawn
fertilizer containing phosphorus is available upon request only for uses
permitted by §
95.06.
   (C)   Effective July 1, 2006, a sign containing the regulations set forth in
this ordinance and the effects of phosphorus on the Rio Ruidoso's water must be
prominently displayed where lawn fertilizers are sold.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.08 ENFORCEMENT.
   Violations of this chapter will be enforced by the Environmental Health
Section of the Public Health Division, Department of Human Services.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.09 SEVERABILITY CLAUSE.
   If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase, or portion of this
chapter or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is declared
invalid or unconstitutional by the decision of a court of competent
jurisdiction, the remainder of this chapter shall be severed therefrom and
shall remain in full force and effect.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.10 EFFECTIVE DATE.
   The stormwater pollution prevention-phosphorus establishing regulations for
lawn fertilizer application and sale chapter of the City of Ruidoso Downs shall
become effective five days after publication as provided by law.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 95.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who violates any section of this chapter for which no
penalty is set out shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   Any person who violates §
95.05 in the application of fertilizer at his or her residence shall be subject
to a fine of up to $50 but not less than $25 per violation. Any commercial
fertilizer applicator, residential or commercial developer, industrial or
commercial owner, or other person who violates §
95.05, and any person who violates §
95.07, shall be subject to a fine of up to $250, but not less than $50, for the
first violation within a 12-month period, up to $350, but not less than $75 for
the second violation within a 12-month period, and up to $500, but not less
than $100 for the third and each subsequent violation within a 12-month period.
(Ord. 2006-01, passed 5-30-2006)
CHAPTER 96: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION
Section
   
96.01   Definitions
   
96.02   Labeling of phosphate content of detergents
   
96.03   Limitation on sale of detergents
   
96.04   Authority
   
96.05   Severability
 
   
96.99   Penalty
§ 96.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   DAIRY EQUIPMENT, BEVERAGE EQUIPMENT and FOOD PROCESSING EQUIPMENT. That
equipment used in the production of milk and dairy products, foods and
beverages, including the processing, preparation or packaging thereof for
consumption.
   INDUSTRIAL CLEANING EQUIPMENT. Machinery and other tools used in cleaning
processes during the course of industrial manufacturing, production and
assembly.
   MACHINE DISHWASHER. Equipment manufactured for the purpose of cleaning
dishes, glassware and other utensils involved in food preparation, consumption
or use, using a combination of water agitation and high temperatures.
   POLYPHOSPHATE BUILDER or PHOSPHORUS. A water softening and soil suspending
agent made from condensed phosphates, including pyrophosphates, tri-phosphates,
tripolyphosphates, metaphosphates and glassy phosphates, used as a detergent
ingredient, but shall not include "polyphosphate builders" or "phosphorus"
which is essential for medical, scientific or special engineering use under
such conditions and regulations as may be prescribed, after hearing, by the
City Administrator.
   RECOMMENDED USE LEVEL. The amount of synthetic detergent or detergent which
the manufacturer thereof recommends for use per wash load, at which level such
synthetic detergent or detergent will effectively perform its intended
function.
   SYNTHETIC DETERGENT or DETERGENT. Any cleaning compound which is available
for household use, laundry use, other personal uses or industrial use which is
composed of organic and inorganic compounds including soaps, water softeners,
surface active agents, dispersing agents, foaming agents, buffering agents,
builders, fillers, dyes, enzymes and fabric softeners, whether in the form of
crystals, powders, flakes, bars, liquids, sprays or any other form.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 96.02 LABELING OF PHOSPHATE CONTENT OF DETERGENTS.
   No person, firm or corporation shall sell, offer or expose for sale, give or
furnish any synthetic detergent or detergent, whether in the form of crystals,
powders, flakes, bars, liquids, sprays or any other form in the City after
September 1, 2006 unless the container, wrapper or other packaging thereof
shall be clearly labeled with respect to its polyphosphate builder or
phosphorus ingredient content clearly and legibly set forth thereon in terms of
percentage of phosphorus by weight, expressed as elemental phosphorus per
container, wrapper or other packaging thereof, as well as grams of phosphorus,
expressed as elemental phosphorus per recommended use level.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 5-30-2006) Penalty, see §
96.99
§ 96.03 LIMITATION ON SALE OF DETERGENTS.
   (A)   No person, firm or corporation shall sell, offer or expose for sale,
give or furnish any synthetic detergent or detergent containing more than 2-1/
2% of phosphorus by weight, expressed as elemental phosphorus, within the City
after September 1, 2006. Additionally, no person, firm or corporation shall
sell, offer or expose for sale, give or furnish any synthetic detergent or
detergent which requires a recommended use level of such synthetic detergent or
detergent which contains more than seven grams of phosphorus by weight
expressed as elemental phosphorus, within the City after September 1, 2006.
Regarding concentrated gel pacs and or tablets no person, firm or corporation
shall sell, offer or expose for sale, give or furnish any synthetic detergent
or detergent containing more than 8.7% or two grams of phosphorus by weight,
expressed as elemental phosphorus, with the City after September 1, 2006.
Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions herein, synthetic detergents or
detergents manufactured for use in commercial machine dishwashers, dairy
equipment, beverage equipment, food processing equipment and industrial
cleaning equipment shall not be subject to the limitations herein set forth but
are hereby made expressly to the provisions of division (B) hereof.
   (B)   No later than September 1, 2006, all individuals, businesses or other
establishments that own or operate a machine designed for commercial or high
capacity machine dishwashing, cleaning dairy equipment, cleaning beverage
equipment, cleaning food processing equipment or industrial cleaning and that
use a specially engineered mix of two or more chemicals to clean dishes shall
obtain an annual phosphorus permit from the City Licensing, Permitting, and
Planning Department. The fee for this permit shall be $25 and following the
initial permit, shall be obtained by the January 31 on every calendar year. In
order to use a synthetic detergent or detergent containing phosphorus,
expressed as elemental phosphorus, the permitted establishment must, on an
annual basis, have a machine manufacturer-certified or recognized professional
inspect and verify that the machine is set to a site specific recommended use
level in order to use the least amount of phosphorus-containing detergent as is
necessary to clean the soiled items to New Mexico Health Department or other
regulatory standards for their applicable uses. A written record of each
inspection shall be kept and signed by the abovementioned professional The
permit and machine inspection records shall be physically kept on the premises
and the City shall inspect all permitted establishments annually for such
records.
   (C)   The concentration of phosphorus by weight, expressed as elemental
phosphorus in any synthetic detergent or detergents shall be determined by the
current applicable method prescribed by the American Society for Testing and
Materials (A.S.T.M.).
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 5-30-2006) Penalty, see §
96.99
§ 96.04 AUTHORITY.
   As per §§ 3-12-2, 3-12-3, 3-17-1, 74-6-1 through 74-6-17 NMSA 1978 and as
per 40 C.F.R. pts 402–403.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 96.05 SEVERABILITY.
   If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase, or portion of this
chapter or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is declared
invalid or unconstitutional by the decision of a court of competent
jurisdiction, the remainder of this chapter shall be severed therefrom and
shall remain in full force and effect.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 5-30-2006)
§ 96.99 PENALTY.
   Any person or business found guilty of violating, disobeying, omitting,
failing to obtain necessary permit, neglecting or refusing to comply with, or
resisting or opposing the enforcement of any provision of this chapter, except
when otherwise specifically provided, shall be fined not less than $50 and not
more than $250 for the first offense, and not less than $100 and not more than
$500 for the second and each subsequent offense, in any one-year period. A
separate and distinct offense shall be regarded as committed each day on which
such person shall continue or permit any such violation or failure to comply is
permitted to exist after notification thereof.
(Ord. 2006-02, passed 5-30-2006)

§ 110.01 BUSINESS REGISTRATION FEE IMPOSED.
   There is imposed on each place of business conducted in this Municipality a
business registration fee of $35. The fee is imposed pursuant to § 3-38-3 NMSA
1978 as it now exists or is amended and shall be known as the “business
registration fee.” The business registration fee may not be pro-rated for
business conducted for a portion of the year.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-1) (Ord. 2022-01, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 110.02 EXEMPTION.
   No business registration fees shall be imposed on any business which is
licensed under
Ch. 111 of this Code, pursuant to § 3-38-1 NMSA 1978.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-2)
§ 110.03 APPLICATION TO DO BUSINESS.
   Any person proposing to engage in business within the Municipal limits of
the City after July 1, 1986 shall apply for and pay a business registration fee
for each outlet, branch, or location within the Municipal limits of the City
prior to engaging in business, unless that person is required to obtain a
business license under
Chapter 111 of this code, or is required to obtain a temporary merchant’s
permit under §
111.17 of this Code. The business registration fee shall be paid to the
Planning and Zoning Department during the regular business hours of the
Administrative Center of the City, as those hours may from time to time be
determined. The application for the permit shall be made three days prior to
the commencement of business or three days prior to the opening of any outlet,
branch, or additional location within the Municipal limits of the City.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-3) (Ord. 2022-01, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 110.04 RENEWAL.
   Prior to December 31st of each year, any person with a place of business in
the City and subject to this chapter shall apply for renewal of business
registration with the Planning and Zoning Department.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-4) (Ord. 2022-01, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 110.05 APPLICATION CONTENT.
   Any person filing an application for issuance or renewal of any business
registration shall include in the application his or her current Revenue
Division taxpayer identification number or evidence of application for a
current Revenue Division taxpayer identification number.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-5) Penalty, see §
110.99
§ 110.06 LATE PAYMENT; NON-PAYMENT.
   (A)   Any person subject to the business registration fee and engaged in
business within the Municipal limits of the City for more than 30 days without
applying for and paying a business registration fee shall be subject to a late
payment penalty of no more than $10 per year. Any person with a place of
business in the City subject to the business registration fee, who does not,
prior to March 16 of each year, renew and pay the business registration fee
shall be subject to a late payment penalty of $10 per year.
   (B)   Any person, firm, or corporation operating without paying the business
registration fee as required herein shall be subject to proceedings in the
Municipal Court of the City. Complaints alleging non-payment of the business
registration fee as required herein may be filed by the Planning and Zoning
Department or the City Attorney.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-6) (Ord. 94-09, passed - -; Ord. 2002-04, passed 5-14-2002;
Ord. 2022-01, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
110.99
Statutory reference:
   Late fee, see § 3-38-5.B(4) NMSA 1978
§ 110.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who shall violate any provision of this chapter for which
no other penalty is provided shall be subject to penalties as provided in §
10.99 of this Code.
   (B)   Upon conviction of non-payment of the business registration fee as
required herein, the person, firm, or corporation shall be fined not less than
$50 nor more than $100.
(1988 Code, § 8-1-6) (Ord. 94-09, passed - -)
CHAPTER 111: GENERAL BUSINESS LICENSING

Appendix A:   Business License Fees
**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 111.01 POLICY.
   The Council hereby declares that the licensing and regulation of certain
businesses not otherwise exempt by law is conducive to the promotion of the
health and general welfare of the City and hereby imposes a license fee and a
separate license on each place of business as conducted by the same person,
firm, corporation, or association. The Council hereby finds the fees enumerated
in this title reasonably related to the expense of regulating the business
therein described and issuing licenses.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-1)
§ 111.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   EXHIBITION. Circuses, menageries, carnivals, side shows, and other similar
amusement enterprises which are open to the public, for which an admission fee
is charged, and which are operated for profit.
   JUNK SHOP. Includes any enterprise engaged in the processing of junk, waste,
discarded, or salvaged materials, machinery, or equipment, including automobile
wrecking and dismantling.
   MOTORCYCLE RENTAL SHOP. Any person who rents a motor vehicle having a seat
or saddle for use of the rider and designed to travel on not more than three
wheels in contact with the ground, but excluding tractors.
   PAWNBROKER. Includes every person who makes a business of lending money on
the security of personal property deposited in his or her keeping.
   SEASONAL MERCHANT. Any person engaging in or intending to engage in the sale
of goods or services sold by a business being operated in the City limits for
more than 72 hours but less than six consecutive months and from a fixed, non-
mobile unit.
   SECONDHAND STORE. Includes every person who deals in the purchase and sale
of goods of any type that have been used or previously sold at retail one or
more times.
   TEMPORARY MERCHANT. Any person engaging in or intending to engage in the
sale of goods or services sold by a business being operated in the City limits
for less than 72 hours or operating out of a vehicle, truck, trailer, or other
mobile unit.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-2)
§ 111.03 EXCEPTIONS.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any secondhand store
operated by any social, recreational, patriotic, benevolent, or athletic
organization, any organization operating a secondhand business for non-profit
to members.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-5)
**** LICENSES AND PERMITS ****
§ 111.15 LICENSE FEE IMPOSED; REQUIRED LICENSES.
   (A)   A business license fee of not less than $10 nor more than $100, as
determined from year to year by the Council, is hereby imposed on all
pawnbrokers, secondhand stores, and junk shops doing business in the City.
   (B)   Any person engaged in any business listed in
Appendix A of this chapter shall secure a license therefor from the Planning &
Zoning Director and shall pay a license fee according to the schedule in
Appendix A of this chapter.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-3) (Ord. 2022-03, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.16 LICENSE REFUSAL OR REVOCATION.
   (A)   For the purpose of regulation, the Council may refuse or revoke a
license.
   (B)   If, at any time after the issuance of a license or permit under this
chapter, it becomes known that a permittee has received that license in
violation of any provision herein, the City Code Enforcement Officer shall
cause written notice of alleged violations to be served upon the permittee.
      (1)   The written notice shall contain the specific alleged violations
and shall notify the permittee of the City's intent to revoke the license or
permit and/or impose the fine set forth in §
111.99 of this Code.
      (2)   The written notice shall notify the permittee of an informal public
hearing before the City Council, at which time the permittee shall have the
opportunity to refute the alleged violations. This informal public hearing
shall be held at the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting after the
delivery of the written notice to the permittee, but in no event shall the
informal hearing be held within three days of the delivery of the written
notice.
   (C)   At the informal public hearing concerning the refusal or revocation of
a license, the applicant, licensee, or permittee, members of the public, and a
representative of the City shall be allowed to present evidence, either orally
or in writing, relevant to the effect of the business on the health, safety, or
welfare of the citizens of the City. The license shall be refused or revoked if
a majority of the members of the Council find:
      (1)   The business of the applicant, licensee, or permittee is noxious,
offensive, pornographic, unsavory, reprehensible, unacceptable for public view,
atrocious, repulsive, abhorrent, or otherwise detrimental to the health,
safety, or welfare of the citizens of the City;
      (2)   The applicant or licensee is guilty of violating an ordinance of
the City relating to the granting of a license; or
      (3)   The applicant or licensee is guilty of violating any other
ordinances of the City.
   (D)   In the event the alleged violations were committed by a person
receiving a permit under §
111.17 of this Code, the provisions and procedures set forth in divisions (B)
and (C) above shall apply, except that any member of the City Council may call
an emergency meeting, to be held, pursuant to the emergency meetings exception
to the Open Meetings Act, § 10-15-1 NMSA 1978, within 24 hours of the receipt
of the notice of violations by the permittee.
   (E)   All business license applications not granted within 15 days shall,
for purposes herein, be deemed refused.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-4) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.17 TEMPORARY MERCHANT'S PERMIT.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any temporary merchant to vend, sell,
dispose, display, or offer to vend, sell, dispose, or display any goods, wares,
or merchandise within the City without having first obtained a temporary
merchant's permit, as hereinafter provided.
   (B)   A temporary merchant’s permit may be obtained by a temporary merchant
upon making an application for such a permit with the Planning & Zoning
Director during the regular business hours of the City Hall of the City. The
fee for the permit shall be as set forth in
Appendix A of this chapter, payable in advance. The application shall be upon
forms provided by the Planning & Zoning Director and shall show compliance with
the following:
      (1)   The name of the applicant, if an individual; the names of partners,
if a partnership; or the names of the principal officers, if a corporation;
      (2)   Proof of a valid State gross receipts tax identification number;
      (3)   Written permission of the property owner upon which the goods,
wares, or merchandise are to be sold;
      (4)   Written certification of availability of at least two off-street
parking spots; and
      (5)   Written certification that at least two dry chemical fire
extinguishers bearing an A, B, and C rating shall be available on the site
during business hours.
   (C)   A copy of the application for the permit will become a part of the
permanent file, and an additional copy shall be mailed to the Bureau of
Revenue, Taxation Department, this State.
   (D)   Any permit issued pursuant to the provisions of this section shall be
valid for a period of three consecutive days. If at any time during the
duration of the permit it becomes known that the permit has been obtained in
violation of the above provisions, and after the procedures outlined in §
111.16 of this Code have been completed and the permittee has been found to
have violated any of the above provisions, the Planning & Zoning Director shall
revoke the same and the applicant shall not be entitled to any return of the
permit fee arising out of the revocation.
   (E)   Temporary merchants shall be subject to the following:
      (1)   The goods, wares, or merchandise shall be displayed in such a
manner that they will not encroach upon any public right-of-way; and
      (2)   The goods, wares, or merchandise shall be displayed in such a
manner as not to impede motor vehicle traffic or pedestrian traffic, or create
any hazard by obstructing the view of motor vehicle traffic, even if the
merchandise is totally upon the property being used by the permittee.
   (F)   Notwithstanding any contrary provisions of this section, non-profit
organizations of type which would otherwise be recognized by the Internal
Revenue Service as tax exempt organizations shall be allowed to engage in the
business of temporary merchants for purposes of fund raising, provided they
meet all the requirements set forth in divisions (B), (C), and (D) above,
excepting the fee required in division (B), which fee, for purposes of this
provision, shall be in the amount set forth in
Appendix A for non-profit organizations, and further excepting that portion of
division (D) concerning the length of the permit's validity. Permits issued
under this division (F) shall not exceed 14 days.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-8) (Ord. 2022-03, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.18 SEASONAL MERCHANT'S PERMIT.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any seasonal merchant to vend, sell, dispose,
display, or offer to vend, sell, dispose, or display any goods, wares, or
merchandise within the City without having first obtained a seasonal merchant's
permit, as hereinafter provided.
   (B)   A seasonal merchant’s permit may be obtained from the Planning &
Zoning Director as outlined in §
111.17(B) of this Code, except that the fee shall be as set forth in
Appendix A of this chapter for seasonal merchants.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-9) (Ord. 2022-03, passed 2-28-2022) Penalty, see §
111.99
**** ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT ****
§ 111.30 INSPECTION.
   The Fire Chief and Code Enforcement Officer or other designated official
shall be permitted at any reasonable time to inspect any property contained on
the premises of any person licensed under this chapter.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-6) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.31 REMEDIES.
   All remedies provided in of this Code and by State law are of equal
application to this chapter, and the City may use any of them in collecting the
license fee.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-7) Penalty, see §
111.99
§ 111.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who shall violate any provision of this chapter for which
no other penalty is provided shall be subject to penalties as provided in §
10.99 of this Code.
   (B)   Any person, firm, or corporation operating without first obtaining a
license as required by this chapter or otherwise violating any provisions of
this chapter shall be fined not less than $5 nor more than $500 for each
offense, and a separate offense shall be deemed committed on each day during or
on which a violation occurs or continues.
(1988 Code, § 8-2-10)

**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 112.01 DEFINITIONS; ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE LICENSES.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ALCOHOLIC LIQUORS. Include any and all distilled or rectified spirits,
potable alcohol, brandy, whiskey, rum, gin, aromatic bitters bearing the
Federal Internal Revenue strip stamps, or any similar alcoholic beverage,
including all blended or fermented beverages, dilution or mixtures of one or
more of the foregoing containing more than 0.5% alcohol, but excluding
medicinal bitters.
   BEER. Any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or
decoction of barley, malt, and hops or other cereals in water, and shall
include such liquors as porter, beer, ale, and stout.
   CLUB. Any non-profit group, including an auxiliary or subsidiary group,
organized and operated under the laws of this State, with a membership of not
less than 50 members who pay membership dues at the rate of not less than $5
per year and who under the constitution and bylaws of the CLUB shall have all
voting rights and full membership privileges, and which group is the owner,
lessee, or occupant of premises used exclusively for club purposes, which group
the Director finds is operated solely for recreation, social, patriotic,
political, benevolent, or athletic purposes.
   DEPARTMENT. The special investigations division of the Department of Public
Safety when the term is used in reference to the enforcement and investigatory
provisions of the Liquor Control Act and the director of the alcohol and gaming
division of the regulation and licensing department when the term is used in
reference to the Liquor Control Act.
   DIRECTOR. The director of the special investigations division of the
Department of Public Safety when the term is used in reference to the
enforcement and investigatory provisions of the Liquor Control Act and means
the director of the alcohol and gaming division of the regulation and licensing
department when the term is used in reference to the licensing provisions of
the Liquor Control Act.
   DISPENSER. Any person licensed under the provisions of the Liquor Control
Act selling, offering for sale, or having in his or her possession with the
intent to sell alcoholic beverages both by the drink for consumption on the
licensed premises and in unbroken packages for consumption and not for resale
off the licensed premises.
   GOVERNING BODY. The Mayor and elected City Council members or commissioners
of an incorporated Municipality.
   INTOXICATING LIQUORS. Those terms defined as "alcoholic liquors," "spiritous
liquors," "beer," and "wine" in this section.
   PACKAGE. Any immediate container of alcoholic liquors, beer, or wine, which
is filled or packed by the manufacturer or bottler thereof for sale by that
manufacturer or bottler to manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, dispensers,
or clubs.
   PERSON. An individual, corporation, firm, partnership, co-partnership,
association, or legal entity.
   RESTAURANT. Any establishment having a State resident as a proprietor or
manager which is held out to the public as a place where meals are prepared and
served primarily for on-premises consumption to  the general public in
consideration of payment and which has a dining room, a kitchen, and the
employees necessary for preparing, cooking, and serving meals; provided, that
RESTAURANT does not include establishments as defined in regulations
promulgated by the Director as serving only hamburgers, sandwiches, salads, and
other fast foods.
   RETAILER. Any person licensed under the provisions of the Liquor Control Act
selling, offering for sale, or having in his or her possession with the intent
to sell any alcoholic beverages in unbroken packages for consumption and not
for resale off the premises.
   SPIRITUOUS LIQUORS. All alcoholic liquors as defined herein, except
fermented beverages such as wine, beer, and ale.
   WHOLESALER. Any person whose place of business is located in this State and
who sells, offers for sale, or possesses for the purpose of sale, any alcoholic
liquor for resale by the purchaser of same.
   WINE. Includes the words "fruit juices" and shall mean all alcoholic
beverages obtained by the fermentation of the natural sugar contained in the
fruit or other agricultural products, with or without the addition of sugar or
other products, and which does not contain less than 0.5% nor more than 21%
alcohol by volume.
(1988 Code, § 8-3-1) (Ord. 93-05, passed - -)

   (A)   Pursuant to the provisions of § 7-24-1 NMSA 1978, on or after the
effective date of this section, no person who has been issued a State license
from the Department shall be given possession of the license by the
Municipality until the person has paid the Municipal license fee as follows:
      (1)   Payment in full by July 1; or
      (2)   In lieu thereof, if the applicant elects to pay biannual

   (B)   The tax rates shall be:

      (3)   Special dispenser's permit: $250;

      (5)   Restaurant license: $250.
   (C)   Persons granted a special dispenser's permit, under the provisions of
§ 60-6A-12 NMSA 1978, shall pay to the Municipality a fee of $10 per day for
each day the permittee dispenses alcoholic beverages.

   (B)   Any person holding a retailer's, dispenser's, or club license from the

may be, evidencing payment of the license tax in accordance with the provisions

license tax as herein provided, that license shall be deemed to have expired.

§ 112.18 LICENSE FEE; TERM; ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER.
   (A)   The annual license fee herein imposed shall embrace the period
commencing on July 1 and expiring on June 30 following. The annual license fee
will not be pro-rated; provided, however, as follows, in conformity with State
law, anything herein to the contrary notwithstanding:
      (1)   A license issued prior to the first day of October shall be subject
to the full amount of the annual license fee;
      (2)   Licenses issued on or subsequent to the first day of October and
prior to the first day of January following shall be subject to three-fourths
of the annual fee;
      (3)   Licenses issued on or subsequent to the first day of January and
prior to the first day of April of a year shall be subject to one-half of the
annual license fee; and
      (4)   Licenses issued on or subsequent to the first day of April of a
year shall be subject to one-fourth of the annual license fee.
   (B)   Revocation or suspension of any retailer's, dispenser's, or club
license shall not entitle the licensee to the refund of any portion of the City
license fee paid, nor shall the licensee be relieved in any way of the
obligation for the payment of any deferred biannual installment thereof.
   (C)   In case of the assignment or transfer of any license, as provided by
law, no refund shall be made by the City to the original licensee, but the
assignment and transfer shall vest in the assignee and transferee the right to
operate under the license tax so paid by the original licensee for the period
covered by the paid license tax and to pay the balance of the license tax upon
the same terms and conditions as if the assignee or transferee were the
original licensee.

§ 112.35 LIQUOR USE AND DISPENSING; LOCATION RESTRICTIONS.
   It shall be unlawful to drink or use intoxicating liquors, or for any person
who is the owner or operator to sell, serve, or furnish, or permit the drinking
or use of any alcoholic liquors in any public dance hall, pool room, bowling
alley, street, or State or Federal building, or in any other public place,
excepting establishments having a license to dispense alcoholic liquors. It
shall also be unlawful for any establishment having a license to dispense
alcoholic liquor to give "curb service" or to serve or sell liquor in any
manner outside of the building on the premises at which the business is
operated.
(1988 Code, § 8-3-8) Penalty, see §
112.99
§ 112.36 OPENING HOURS.
   (A)   The licenses of retailers of alcoholic liquors shall allow them to
sell and deliver alcoholic liquors, and the licenses of dispensers of alcoholic
liquors and club liquor licenses shall allow them to sell, serve, deliver, and
permit the consumption of alcoholic liquors on the licensed premises:
      (1)   On Mondays from 7:00 a.m. until midnight;
      (2)   On other weekdays from after midnight of the previous day until 2:
00 a.m., then from 7:00 a.m. until midnight; and
      (3)   On Sundays after midnight of the previous day until 2:00 a.m., and
then from 12:00 noon until 12:00 midnight.
   (B)   Dispensers, retail, and club licensees shall close their places of
business during voting hours on the day of the biennial primary election of
each even-numbered year, on the day of the biennial general election held upon
the first Tuesday of November of each even-numbered year, on the days of the
City elections for City officers, and on the days of those other elections as
may be prescribed by rules and regulations promulgated by the Director of the
Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control.
   (C)   It is unlawful for any licensed retailer of alcoholic liquors to sell
or deliver alcoholic liquors or for any licensed dispenser or club to sell,
deliver, serve, or permit the consumption of alcoholic liquors on his or her
licensed premises during hours other than those described by this section.
(1988 Code, § 8-3-13) Penalty, see §
112.99
