§ 113.01 GENERAL PROVISIONS.
   (A)   This chapter may be cited as the "Tattoo and Body Piercing Act" ("this
chapter").
   (B)   This chapter provides for the licensing and regulation of tattoo and
body piercing studios and temporary locations.
   (C)   No person shall perform or offer to perform any tattooing or body
piercing unless the tattooing or body piercing shall be done in compliance with
this chapter.
   (D)   No person may cause, suffer, or allow the operation, management, or
maintenance of a tattoo or body piercing studio or temporary location without a
current, valid, and unsuspended license issued in accordance with this chapter.
   (E)   All tattoo and body piercing studios and temporary locations shall
comply with the minimum standard specified in this chapter in addition to any
other applicable ordinances, statutes, rules and regulations.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ANTISEPTIC. An agent that kills disease-causing microorganisms on human skin
or mucosa.
   ARTIST. A person who performs tattooing and/or body piercing, and who shall
be responsible for complying with the provisions of these sections.
   ASEPTIC TECHNIQUE. A hygienic practice, which prevents and hinders the
direct transfer of microorganisms, regardless of pathogenicity, from one person
or place to another person or place.
   BODY PIERCER. A person who performs body piercing and who shall be
responsible for adherence to the provisions of these sections; hereafter
referred to as ARTIST.
   BODY PIERCING. The creation of an opening in an individual's body to insert
jewelry or another decoration, but not including either ear piercing or
practices considered to be medical procedures by the New Mexico Board of
Medical Examiners.
   BODY PIERCING STUDIO. A permanent, non-dwelling building or portion of a
building, designated by a license holder and located in accordance with
applicable local zoning codes where body piercing is performed, completely
separated from living quarters; hereafter referred to as STUDIO.
   CLIENT. A person requesting the application of a tattoo or body piercing.
   CONTAMINATED WASTE. Any liquid or semi-liquid blood or other potentially
infectious materials; contaminated items that would release blood or other
potentially infectious materials in a liquid or semi-liquid state if
compressed; items that are caked with dried blood or other potentially
infectious materials and are capable of releasing these materials during
handling; contaminated sharps and pathological and microbiological wastes
containing blood and other potentially infectious material, as defined in 29
C.F.R. pt 1910.1030, known as "Occupational Exposure to Bloodborne Pathogens"
as such may be replaced or amended from time to time. Copies of this provision
are indexed and filed in the office of the City Clerk, and are available for
inspection during normal working hours.
   DEPARTMENT. The Licensing, Permit. and Planning Department or such other
department or departments as may be designated by the City Administrator.
   DISINFECTANT. An agent that kills disease-causing microorganisms or
inanimate objects or surfaces.
   EAR PIERCING. The creation of an opening in an individual's ear, not
including any cartilage, with an ear piercing gun.
   EAR PIERCING GUN. A device that pierces an individual's ear using a single-
use stud and clasp ear piercing system. An ear-piercing gun shall not be used
to pierce any other part of the body besides the ear.
   GERMICIDAL SOAP. An agent designed for use on the skin that kills disease-
causing microorganisms, including but not limited to, products containing
povidone-iodine, chloroxylenol, triclosan, and chlothexidine gluconate.
   GERMICIDAL SOLUTION. An agent that kills disease-causing microorganisms on
hard surfaces; a disinfectant or sanitizer registered with the Environmental
Protection Agency and/or an approximate 1:100 dilution of household chlorine
bleach (one-quarter cup bleach and one gallon of water).
   HAND WASHING FACILITY. A sink equipped with hot and cold or tempered running
water under pressure, used for washing hands, arms, or other portions of the
body.
   HEALTH CARE PRACTITIONER. A person licensed by the state to practice
medicine.
   INSTRUMENTS. Hand pieces, needles, needle bars, hemostats, forceps, pliers,
and other items that may come in contact with a client's body or possible
exposure to bodily fluids during tattoo and body piercing procedures.
   JEWELRY. Any personal ornament inserted into a pierced area, which must be
made of surgical implant grade stainless steel (minimum of 316L or 316LVM),
solid 14k or 18k gold, niobium, titanium (minimum of 6A14V), or platinum, which
is free of nicks, scratches, or irregular surfaces and has been property
sterilized prior to use.
   LEGAL GUARDIAN. A person, licensed child-placing agency, or authorized
agency designated by a court as having the right to possession of the child and
the right to consent to medical, surgical, dental, and psychological treatment
of the child.
   LICENSE HOLDER. A person who owns, operates, or maintains a tattoo studio,
tattoo and body piercing studio, body piercing studio or temporary location in
compliance with these sections.
   SANITIZE. To treat a clean surface and kill pathogenic microorganisms.
   SCARIFICATION. The cutting into the skin with a sharp instrument or branding
the skin with a heated or cooled instrument to produce a permanent mark or
design on the skin.
   SHARPS. Any object (sterile or contaminated) that may purposefully or
accidentally cut or penetrate the skin or mucosa including, but not limited to,
needles, scalpel blades, and razor blades.
   SHARPS CONTAINER. A puncture-resistant, leak-proof container that can be
closed for handling, storage, transportation, and disposal and that is labeled
with the international biohazard symbol.
   SINGLE-USE. Articles intended for one-time, one-person use and which are to
be discarded after such use. All needles used in tattooing or body piercing
shall be disposable single-use.
   TATTOO/TATTOOING. The practice of producing an indelible mark or figure on
the human body by scarification or by depositing pigment into the epidermis
using needles, scalpels, or other related devices including, but not limited to
intradermal cosmetics, dermography, micropigmentation, permanent color
technology, and micropigmentation implantation, but does not include practices
that are considered medical procedures by the New Mexico Board of Medical
Examiners.
   TATTOO AND BODY PIERCING AREA. The portion of the tattoo or body piercing
studio or temporary location used for applying tattoos or performing body
piercing, including all surrounding areas which are likely to come into contact
with contaminated waste.
   TATTOO STUDIO. A permanent, nondwelling building or portion of a building,
designated by a license holder and located in accordance with applicable local
zoning codes where tattooing is performed, completely separated from living
quarters; hereafter referred to as STUDIO.
   TATTOOIST. A person who performs tattooing and who is responsible for
adherence to the provisions of these sections; hereafter referred to as ARTIST.
   TEMPORARY LOCATION. A fixed location at which tattooing or body piercing is
performed for a specified length of time of not more than seven days in
conjunction with a single event or celebration, where the primary function of
the event or celebration is tattooing or body piercing.
   UNIVERSAL PRECAUTIONS. A method of infection control in which employees
treat all blood and body fluids as to contain all bloodborne pathogens and
taking proper precautions to prevent the spread of any bloodborne pathogens.
Precautions include hand washing, gloving, personal protective equipment,
injury prevention, and proper handling and disposal of needles, other sharp
instruments, and blood and body fluid contaminated products.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.03 PHYSICAL FACILITIES.
   (A)   A studio must be in a permanent, nondwelling building or portion of a
building located in conformity with applicable zoning codes, if any. The studio
shall be separated from any living quarters by complete floor to ceiling
partitioning and shall contain no access to living quarters.
   (B)   The studio or temporary location shall be maintained in a sanitary
condition.
      (1)   Work surfaces shall be cleaned and sanitized with a germicidal
solution.
      (2)   Other environmental surfaces shall be cleaned with an all-purpose
detergent disinfectant.
   (C)   The walls, ceilings, and floors shall be kept in good repair. The
tattoo and body piercing area shall be constructed of smooth, hard, surfaces
that are non-porous, free of open holes or cracks, light colored, and easily
cleaned. New studios shall not include dark-colored surfaces in the tattoo and
body piercing area. Existing studios with dark-colored surfaces in the tattoo
and body piercing area shall replace the dark-colored surfaces with light-
colored surfaces whenever the facilities are remodeled.
   (D)   Studios or temporary locations shall have adequate lighting of at
least 50 foot candles of illumination in the tattooing and body piercing areas.
   (E)   Adequate mechanical ventilation shall be provided in the studio.
   (F)   Each studio or temporary location shall be equipped with hand-washing
facilities for its personnel with unobstructed access to the tattoo and body
piercing area such that artists can return to the area without having to touch
anything with their hands. Hand-washing facilities shall be equipped with hot
and cold or tempered running water under pressure; liquid germicidal soap;
single-use towels or other approved hand-drying devices; and a covered refuse
container. Such facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair.
   (G)   Animals are not permitted in the studios or temporary locations,
except for:
      (1)   Guide or service animals accompanying persons with disabilities;
      (2)   Nonmammalian animals in enclosed glass containers such as fish
aquariums, which shall be outside the tattooing and body piercing area; and
      (3)   The application of an identification tattoo upon a pet which
tattooing shall be performed in a room completely separated from all areas used
for the tattooing and/or body piercing of humans.
   (H)   Use of tobacco products shall be prohibited in the tattoo and body
piercing area. Consumption of alcoholic beverages shall be prohibited in the
studio or temporary location.
   (I)   The studio or temporary location shall be kept free of rodents and
vermin arid protected from infestation by insects.
   (J)   If tattooing or body piercing is performed where cosmetology services
are provided, the tattooing or body piercing shall be performed in an enclosed
area that is separated from the other uses.
   (K)   Each studio or temporary location shall have a tattoo and body
piercing area, which is screened from public view for clients requesting
privacy.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.04 PERSONNEL RESPONSIBILITIES.
   (A)   All artists while tattooing or body piercing shall wear clean outer
garments, maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness, and conform to
hygienic practices while on duty.
   (B)   All artists shall wash their hands thoroughly using hot or tempered
water with a liquid germicidal soap before and after tattooing or body piercing
and as often as necessary to remove contaminants.
   (C)   All artists must wear single-use examination gloves while assembling
tattooing and body piercing instruments and while tattooing and body piercing.
   (D)   At a minimum, the artist's examination gloves shall be discarded after
the completion of each procedure on an individual client.
   (E)   When a session is interrupted or immediately after an artist's glove
is perforated, pierced, torn, or other contaminated:
      (1)   Gloves shall be removed and properly discarded;
      (2)   Hands shall be thoroughly washed as described in division (B),
above; and
      (3)   A fresh pair of gloves used.
   (F)   Artists shall use universal precautions while tattooing or body
piercing.
   (G)   The area of the client's skin to be tattooed shall be cleaned with an
approved germicidal soap according to label directions.
   (H)   The external skin of the client to be pierced shall be cleaned with an
approved germicidal soap according to label directions. In the case of oral
piercings, the operator shall provide the individual with antiseptic mouthwash
in a single-use cup and shall ensure that the individual utilizes the mouthwash
provided. In the case of a lip, labret, or cheek piercing, procedures described
for both skin and oral piercings shall be followed.
   (I)   If shaving is required, razors shall be disposable single-use.
   (J)   All procedures shall be performed using aseptic technique.
   (K)   Upon request of the City, an artist shall provide the City with proof
that the artist has:
      (1)   Either completed or was offered and declined, in writing, the
Hepatitis B vaccination series; or
      (2)   Antibody testing has revealed that the artist is immune to
Hepatitis B; or
      (3)   The vaccine is contraindicated for medical reasons.
Contraindication requires a dated and signed physician's statement specifying
the name of the artist and that the vaccine cannot be given.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.05 STERILIZATION.
   (A)   A studio or temporary location is required to utilize instruments that
have been prepared as described in this chapter. The studio or temporary
location shall use sterilization equipment that is approved by the United
States Food and Drug Administration for the purpose of sterilization, is
adequate in size to accommodate necessary utensils and instruments, and is in
proper working order. A copy of the manufacturer's recommended procedures for
operation of the sterilization unit(s) must be available for inspection by the
City. The equipment shall be used according to the manufacturer's recommended
procedures for the operation of the unit(s).
   (B)   Sterilized instruments stored in an approved manner and not used with
30 days after sterilization shall no longer be considered sterile and shall be
resterilized before use, unless the studio or temporary location utilizes
presterilized instruments sterilized by the manufacturer. If presterilized
instruments are used, the artist shall obtain documentation from the
manufacturer that describes the method of sterilization utilized by the
manufacturer and the manufacturer's recommendations for storage and maintenance
of sterility. This documentation shall be available for inspection by the City.
The artist shall follow the manufacturer's instructions for storage and
maintenance of sterility.
   (C)   One of the following methods of sterilization shall be used.
      (1)   Autoclave - steam under pressure:
         (a)   One hundred and twenty-one degrees Celsius (250 degrees
Fahrenheit) and a pressure of at least 15 pounds per square inch for not less
than 30 minutes after the camber of the autoclave has reached the required
temperature and pressure; or
         (b)   As specified in the manufacturer's operator's manual.
      (2)   Dry heat sterilization:
         (a)   One hundred and sixty degrees Celsius (320 degrees Fahrenheit)
for not less than one hour under atmospheric pressure after the sterilizer has
reached the required temperature; or
         (b)   As specified in the manufacturer's operator's manual.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.06 TATTOOING AND BODY PIERCING INSTRUMENTS AND JEWELRY.
   (A)   Instruments and jewelry used during tattooing and piercing procedures
which may contact blood or other bodily fluids, or which come in direct contact
with skin which is not intact shall be sterilized after each use or disposed
of. These devices include, but are not limited to, needles, bars, tubes,
forceps, receiving tubes and tapers. This does not include ear piercing guns or
tattoo machines/devices.
   (B)   Instruments and jewelry used during tattooing and body piercing which
do not come in contact with broken skin but may come in contact with mucous
membranes and oral tissue should be sterilized after each use. If, however,
sterilization is not feasible because the instrument or jewelry will be
damaged, the instrument or jewelry shall be treated with a germicidal solution
prior to use. These devices include, but are not limited to, calipers and gauge
wheels.
   (C)   Instruments that come into contact only with intact skin shall be
treated with a germicidal solution prior to use. These devices may include, but
are not limited to, hand mirrors.
   (D)   Reusable instruments shall be constructed in a manner that permits
easy cleaning and sterilization.
   (E)   Needles used to perform tattooing or body piercing shall be single-use
and disposed of in a sharps container.
   (F)   Single-use disposable instruments shall be maintained in clean
condition and dispensed in a manner to prevent contamination to the unused
instruments. These devices include, but are not limited to, cups, cotton swabs,
corks, rubber bands, and toothpicks.
   (G)   Use of styptic pens or alum solids to control blood flow is
prohibited.
   (H)   All dyes or pigments used in tattooing and piercing shall be non-
toxic, free from adulteration, and made from materials generally regarded as
safe. Marking instruments shall be single-use or sanitized by design, such as
alcohol based ink pens, and shall be used only on intact skin that has been
treated with a germicidal soap. Any marking instrument that comes in contact
with mucous membranes or broken skin shall be single-use.
   (I)   Only single-use pigment or dye containers shall be used for each
client. Pigments and dyes shall be dispensed from containers in a manner to
prevent contamination to the unused portion. Individual containers of dye or
pigment shall be discarded after use.
   (J)   In order to minimize transmission of body fluids and disease, single-
use plastic covers shall be used to cover spray bottles or other reusable
accessories for multiple client use that are handled by the artist during
tattooing and body piercing.
   (K)   All stencils shall be single-use. Petroleum jellies, soaps,
antiperspirants, and other products used in the application of stencils shall
be dispensed and applied using aseptic technique and in a manner to prevent
contamination of the original container and its contents. The applicator shall
be single-use.
   (L)   Contaminated reusable instruments shall be placed in a labeled covered
container which may contain a disinfectant solution until the instruments can
be cleaned and sterilized.
   (M)   All containers holding contaminated instruments and container lids
shall be emptied of contaminated solution and cleaned and sanitized daily or
more often if needed.
   (N)   Reusable instruments shall be cleaned by gloved personnel prior to
sterilization by one of the following methods:
      (1)   Mechanically pre-clean the items by using a clean cotton ball or
swab moistened with a solution of low-residue detergent and cool water, with
care taken to ensure the removal of any pigment or body substances not visible
to the eye, thoroughly rinse with warm water and then drain, and clean by
soaking in a protein dissolving detergent-enzyme cleaner used according to
manufacturer's instructions; or
      (2)   Clean the items in an ultrasonic cleaning unit used according to
manufacturer's instruction. A copy of the manufacturer's recommended procedures
for operation of the ultrasonic cleaning unit must be available for inspection
by the City; and
      (3)   Rinse and dry the items prior to packaging for sterilization.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.07 DISPOSAL OF INFECTIOUS WASTE.
   Contaminated waste which may release liquid blood or body fluids when
compressed or may release dried blood or body fluids when handled must be
placed in an approved "red" bag which is marked with the international
"biohazard" symbol. It must then be disposed of by a waste hauler approved by
the State of New Mexico or, at a minimum pursuant to the requirements of 29
C.F.R. pt 1910.1030, as it may be amended from time to time. Sharps ready for
disposal shall be disposed of in approved sharps containers. Contaminated waste
which does not release liquid blood or body fluids when compressed or does not
release dried blood or body fluids when handled may be placed in a covered
receptacle and disposed of through normal, approved disposal methods. Storage
of contaminated waste on-site shall not exceed the period specified by the
State of New Mexico or more than a maximum of 30 days, as specified in 29
C.F.R. pt 1910.1030, whichever is stricter.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.08 CLIENT QUALIFICATIONS, DISCLOSURE, AND RECORDS.
   (A)   Except as permitted in division (C) of this section, a client must be
a minimum of 18 years of age. All clients shall present at the time of
tattooing or body piercing a valid, government issued, positive identification
card including, but not limited to, a driver's license, passport, or military
identification. The identification must contain a photograph of the individual
and a printed date of birth.
   (B)   The artist shall verify and document in the permanent client record
the client's age, date of birth, and the type of identification provided.
   (C)   (1)   An artist may not perform tattooing or body piercing on a person
younger than 18 years of age without both:
         (a)   Obtaining a notarized informed consent form from a parent or
legal guardian of the minor; and
         (b)   Having the parent or legal guardian present before and during
the administering the tattoo or body piercing.
      (2)   The parent or legal guardian shall personally deliver the notarized
informed consent and shall remain present throughout the administration of the
tattoo or body piercing. Delivery of the informed consent by the person who is
under 18 years of age is not sufficient to permit the administration of the
tattoo or body piercing. Photographic identification of the parent or legal
guardian is required. Such photographic identification of the parent or
guardian shall meet the same standards as is required of a client's
identification in division (A), above.
   (D)   An operator or employee shall refuse to provide body art services to a
client who is or appears to be intoxicated on alcohol or drugs.
   (E)   Tattooing and body piercing shall not be performed on any skin surface
which manifests any evidence of unhealthy conditions such as rashes, boils,
open sores, infections, or abrasions.
   (F)   Before receiving a tattoo, each client (and, if applicable, the
client's parent or legal guardian) shall be informed both verbally and in
writing about the possible risk and dangers associated with the application of
each tattoo. These shall include, but are not limited to, at least the
following:
      (1)   The possibility of discomfort or pain;
      (2)   The permanence of the markings;
      (3)   The risk of infection; and
      (4)   The possibility of allergic reaction to the pigments or other
materials used.
   (G)   Before receiving a body piercing, each client (and, if applicable, the
client's parent or legal guardian) shall be informed verbally and in writing
about the possible risks and dangers associated with receiving a body piercing.
These shall include, but are not limited to, at least the following:
      (1)   The possibility of discomfort or pain;
      (2)   The possibility of scarring;
      (3)   The possibility of bleeding;
      (4)   The possibility of swelling;
      (5)   The risk of infection;
      (6)   The possibility of nerve damage; and
      (7)   The increased risk for adolescents during certain stages of
development.
   (H)   The studio or temporary location shall maintain proper records of each
client. The information shall be permanently recorded and made available for
examination by the City upon request. Records shall be maintained at the studio
tor at least three years following the date of the last entry. The temporary
location client records shall be maintained by the license holder. These
permanent records shall include the following, at a minimum:
      (1)   The name, address, and telephone number of the client;
      (2)   The date tattooing or body piercing was performed;
      (3)   The client's age, date of birth, and the type of positive
identification provided to the artist (this information is to be recorded by
the artist as described in division (B) of this section);
      (4)   The specific color or colors of the tattoo or type of jewelry used
for the piercing and, when available, the manufacturer's catalogue or
identification number of each color or type of jewelry used;
      (5)   The location on the body where the tattoo or body piercing was
performed;
      (6)   The name of the artist(s) performing the tattoo or body piercing;
      (7)   A statement that the client (and, if applicable, the client's
parent or legal guardian) has received a copy of applicable written care
instructions, and that the client has read and understands the instructions;
      (8)   The signature of the client (and, if applicable, the client's
parent or legal guardian);
      (9)   The notarized informed consent of the client's parent or guardian
as specified in division (C) of this section, if applicable; and
      (10)   If applicable, the name, relationship to the client, and type of
positive identification provided to the artist by the client's parent or
guardian.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.09 CARE OF THE NEW TATTOO AND/OR BODY PIERCING.
   (A)   Each time tattooing or body piercing is performed the client (and, if
applicable, the client's parent or legal guardian) shall receive oral and
written instructions on the care of the area tattooed or pierced. The client
(and, if applicable, the client's parent or legal guardian) shall sign a
written statement in the permanent client record acknowledging that the client
has received a copy of the written care instructions, and that the client has
read and understands the instructions.
   (B)   The written care instructions for tattooing shall contain at least the
following items:
      (1)   For at least two weeks, the need to minimize exposure to the sun,
and to discourage swimming in fresh, salt, or chlorinated water;
      (2)   The need to properly cleanse the tattooed area;
      (3)   The need to apply antibiotic ointment or cream;
      (4)   The need to use sterile bandage(s) or other sterile dressing(s)
when necessary;
      (5)   The name of the artist, and the name, address, and telephone number
of the studio or temporary location; and
      (6)   The instructions for the client to consult a health care
practitioner at the first sign of infection or an allergic reaction, and to
report any diagnosed infection, allergic reaction, or adverse reaction
resulting from the application of the tattoo to the artist and to the New
Mexico Department of Health.
   (C)   The written care instructions for body piercing shall contain at least
the following items:
      (1)   The need to properly cleanse the pierced area by using
antibacterial or antimicrobial soap for the external skin and or an antiseptic
or carbamide peroxide mouth wash for the oral cavity;
      (2)   For at least the first two to six weeks, the need to minimize
exposure to the sun, and to discourage swimming in fresh, salt, or chlorinated
water;
      (3)   The need to use sterile bandage(s) or other sterile dressing(s)
when necessary;
      (4)   The name of the artist, and the name, address, and telephone number
of the studio or temporary location; and
      (5)   The instructions for the client to consult a health care
practitioner at the first sign of infection or an allergic reaction, and to
report any diagnosed infection, allergic reaction, or adverse reaction
resulting from the body piercing to the artist and to the New Mexico Department
of Health.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.10 LICENSING FEES; PROCEDURES AND EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   Operator and facility; licenses required.  A person shall not operate
a tattoo and/or body piercing studio or temporary location unless that person
possesses a current, valid, and unsuspended operator license issued by the
department in accordance with the provisions of this chapter and that facility
has a valid, current facility license issued by this department.
   (B)   Operator and facility license fees. 
      (1)   Operator license fees. Each operator (person performing tattooing
and/or body piercing) shall obtain an annual operators license which is valid
for both or either operation (tattooing and body piercing). The fee for this
license shall be $100 per operator per year.
      (2)   Facility license fees. All tattoo and body piercing studios and
temporary locations shall obtain a license annually, or as indicated below,
from the City shall pay a nonrefundable license fee for each place of business
operated as follows:
         (a)   $100 per tattoo only studio license (annual facility license);
         (b)   $100 per tattoo only temporary location facility license (for a
specified length of time not to exceed seven days);
         (c)   $175 per tattoo and body piercing studio license (annual
facility license) – with the fee to be paid as follows: $ 100 for the tattoo
portion; and $75 for the body piercing portion;
         (d)   $175 per tattoo and body piercing temporary location license
(for a specified length of time not to exceed seven days) – with the tee to be
paid as follows: $ 100 for the tattoo portion; and $75 for the body piercing
portion;
         (e)   $100 per body piercing only studio license (annual facility
license); and
         (f)   $100 per body piercing only temporary location license (for a
specified length of time not to exceed seven days).
   (C)   License forms. License forms may be obtained from the Department.
   (D)   License application. A person desiring to operate a tattoo and/or body
piercing studio or temporary location shall apply to the Department for the
issuance of a license. An application shall be submitted for each tattoo studio
or temporary location and a separate application shall be submitted for each
body piercing studio or temporary location. An application shall also be
submitted for each operator (employee who performs tattooing or body piercing.)
The license application for each operator and studio or temporary location
shall be signed and verified, shall be made on the license application
furnished by the Department, and shall contain the following information:
      (1)   The full legal name under which the studio or temporary location is
to be conducted;
      (2)   The address of the studio or temporary location that is to be
licensed. Sufficient descriptive information must be included if the studio or
temporary location is located in a portion of the building with other uses or
license holders;
      (3)   If a proprietorship, the name and residence address of the
proprietor; if a partnership, the names and residence addresses of all
partners; if a corporation, the date and place of incorporation and name and
address of its registered agent in the state; or if any other type of
association, then the type of association and the names and addresses of the
principals of such association;
      (4)   For each studio or temporary location, the name(s) and residence
address(es) of the responsible individual(s) thereof;
      (5)   The name(s) and gender(s) of the studio's or temporary location's
artist(s);
      (6)   The usual days and hours of operation of each studio or temporary
location;
      (7)   A full description of all services to be provided at the studio or
temporary location;
      (8)   The current revenue division taxpayer identification number for the
studio or temporary location; and
      (9)   A copy of a certificate of insurance, issued by a company licensed
and authorized to do business in the State of New Mexico, for general public
liability insurance insuring against such claims naming the tattoo and/or body
piercing studio as the insured with a single aggregate limit in an amount not
less than $300,000. The insurance shall remain in full force and effect during
the duration of the license.
   (E)   Inspection of studios and temporary locations. Prior to the issuance
of a license and prior to the renewal of a license and at such other times as
the Department may deem necessary for the enforcement of this chapter, the
Department shall inspect the studio or temporary location for compliance with
the provisions of this chapter and applicable statutes, rules, regulations, and
zoning codes. Upon request by the Department to a license holder or to his or
her employee or agent in charge of the studio or temporary location, the
license holder or his or her employee or agent shall allow the Department
official, upon presentation of proper identification, to enter the premises,
inspect all parts of the premises and to inspect and copy records of the studio
or temporary location. During an inspection, the Department may take samples of
equipment and supplies on the premises for the purpose of determining
compliance with this chapter. The Department shall return any samples of
equipment or supplies after the investigation is completed. The license holder,
his or her employee or agent shall be given an opportunity to accompany the
Department official on the inspection and to receive a report of the inspection
within 12 business days after the inspection. Refusal to allow an inspection is
grounds for suspension or revocation of the license.
   (F)   Issuance of license. The City may issue a license to the owner of a
studio or temporary location after determining that the studio or temporary
location is in compliance with this chapter and applicable statutes, rules,
regulations and zoning codes.
      (1)   The initial studio (facility) license shall be valid for one year
from the date of issuance, which becomes the anniversary date. The temporary
location license is valid for the specified period, which shall not exceed
seven days.
      (2)   The renewal studio license shall be valid for one year from the
anniversary date.
      (3)   The license shall be displayed in a prominent place in the studio
or temporary location.
   (G)   Renewal of license - applicable to studios only.
      (1)   Each year, the studio or facility license holder shall renew its
license in accordance with the requirements of this section.
      (2)   The license holder shall renew the license by filing an application
for renewal on the form prescribed by the Department accompanied by the
required licensure fee. A licensee must file for renewal before the expiration
date of the current license. A person who files a renewal application after the
expiration date must pay an additional $50 as a delinquency fee.
      (3)   Failure to submit the renewal application annually shall subject
the studio to the enforcement provisions of this chapter
         (a)   Amendment of license. A license must be amended when the name,
ownership, location, or services of the licensed studio is changed. Such
changes require submission of the fees as outlined in division (A) of this
section.
         (b)   Notification of change of location of studio.
            1.   Not fewer than 30 days in advance of the change, the licensee
shall notify the Department in writing of the licensee's intent to change the
location of a licensed studio. The notice shall include the address of the new
location, and the name and residence address of the individual in charge of the
studio at the new location.
            2.   Not later than the tenth day after the change of location is
complete, the license holder shall notify the Department in writing and shall
verify the information submitted under division (G)(3)(b)1. above.
            3.   Notice will be deemed adequate if the licensee provides the
intent and verification notices to Department within the established time
frames of divisions (G)(3)(b) 1. and 2. above by certified mail, return receipt
requested, mailed to the Ruidoso Downs Licensing, Planning, and Permitting
Department, P.O. Box 348, Ruidoso Downs, New Mexico 88346, or such other
address as may be specified by the City.
      (4)   Operator's licenses shall be obtained by a person prior to
performing any tattooing or body piercing. Persons obtaining a new license can
do so throughout the year for that specific calendar year for the full fee.
Licenses must be renewed no later than, of each year.
      (5)   The operator license holder shall renew the license by filing an
application for renewal on the form prescribed by the Department accompanied by
the required licensure fee. A licensee must file for renewal before the
December 31 deadline ("expiration date") date of the current license. A person
who files a renewal application after the expiration date must pay an
additional $50 as a delinquency fee.
      (6)   Failure to submit the renewal application annually shall subject
the studio to the enforcement provisions of this chapter.
   (H)   Exemption from licensure. Persons who engage only in the following are
exempt from the licensing requirements of this section:
      (1)   A location within a medical facility which is licensed under other
law, or an office or clinic of a person licensed by the New Mexico State Board
of Medical Examiners;
      (2)   A person who performs only ear piercing; or
      (3)   A facility in which only ear piercing is performed.
   (I)   Nontransferable. A license for a studio or temporary location shall
not be transferable from one place or person to another.
   (J)   Posting. A studio's or temporary location's license shall be posted in
a conspicuous place within that studio. A person shall not display a license
unless it has been issued to him or her by the Department and has not expired
or been suspended or revoked.
   (K)   Existing studios. All places engaged in tattooing and/or body piercing
before the effective date of this chapter shall have 90 days from the effective
date of this chapter to comply with the license requirements.
   (L)   Penalties. It shall be unlawful for any person to perform or offer to
perform any tattooing or body piercing unless such procedures are performed in
a current City-licensed studio or temporary location with a current, valid, and
unsuspended City-issued operator's license. Each such tattooing or body
piercing procedure shall constitute a separate offense and each day in which a
violation occurs or continues shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004; Ord. 2005-03, passed 2-28-2005)
§ 113.11 REFUSAL, REVOCATION, OR SUSPENSION OF LICENSE AND ENFORCEMENT
PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Basis. The Department may refuse to license a studio or temporary
location or may revoke or suspend a license for a violation or violations of
the requirements of this chapter or for the purpose of regulation and when
deemed to be in the public interest. The Department shall provide the applicant
or license holder with written notice of an adverse determination.
   (B)   Hearing. Except as noted below, a license which had been issued shall
not be suspended or revoked pursuant to this chapter without providing the
license holder an opportunity for an administrative hearing.
   (C)   Immediate suspension. The Department may suspend a license immediately
without prior notice to the license holder if it determines, after inspection,
that conditions at the studio or temporary location present a substantial
danger of illness, serious physical harm or death to persons who might
patronize the studio or temporary location. A suspension action taken pursuant
to this section is effective when communicated to the license holder or an
employees or agent of the license holder who is in charge of the premises
involved. If there is no designated employee or agent in charge of the
premises, communication to an employee physically present of the premises is
sufficient communication to make the suspension effective. Suspension action
taken pursuant to this section shall not continue beyond the time that the
conditions causing the suspension cease to exist, as determined by a Department
inspection at the request of the license holder.
   (D)   Appeal. An applicant or license holder may appeal an adverse
determination of the Department to the Governing Body. The applicant or license
holder shall submit a written request for such a hearing to the office of the
City Administrator within 14 days of the determination from which the appeal is
taken. After providing notice and opportunity for hearing, the majority of the
governing body may affirm, reverse, or modify the determination of the
Department.
   (E)   Enforcement and penalties.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to perform or offer to perform
any tattooing or body piercing unless such procedures are performed or offered
to be performed in compliance with all applicable requirements of this chapter.
The violation of any requirement of this chapter shall constitute a misdemeanor
and shall be punishable as permitted by City Code, as it may be amended from
time to time. Each tattooing or body piercing procedure shall constitute a
separate offense and each day in which a violation occurs or continues shall
constitute a separate offense.
      (2)   The City shall have the right to enforce this chapter through both
its criminal and civil jurisdiction in the Municipal Court of the City of
Ruidoso Downs and the District Court of the State of New Mexico, In the event
of a violation of this chapter, the appropriate authorities of the City, in
addition to other available remedies, may institute injunction, mandamus or
other appropriate action or proceeding to prevent, enjoin, ore remedy such
violation.
   (F)   Re-issuance of a license. If a license issued under these sections has
been revoked or denied for violation of these rules, the license holder named
in the revocation or denial is not eligible for licensing under these sections
for a period of two years.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
§ 113.12 SALE OF SYRINGE NEEDLES TO MINORS UNLAWFUL.
   It shall be unlawful for a person to sell a syringe needle to a minor
without the minor first presenting a prescription issued by a person licensed
to issue such a prescription and which prescription requires the use of such a
syringe needle. It is not a violation of this section for a parent or legal
guardian of minor to provide a syringe needle to that minor. A violation of
this section shall constitute a misdemeanor and shall be punishable as
permitted §
10.99 of the Code, as it may be amended from time to time. Each sale of a
syringe needle to a minor shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004; Ord. 2005-03, passed 2-28-2005)
§ 113.13 AUTOMATIC REPEAL.
   In the event the State of New Mexico enacts regulations or statutes
governing body piercing, tattooing, or artists, this chapter shall be
automatically repealed upon the effective date of the state regulations or
statutes.
(Ord. 2004-06, passed 10-25-2004)
